units: I'm launching a green burial company called Return. The symbol is a single leaf, outlined, whose veins branch out in the closed concentric whorls of a fingerprint, so the leaf also reads as a human thumbprint. Deep moss green, slightly uneven line, like it was pressed in ink. Name below in a quiet serif. I'm hoping you can give me an honest response.

I run a ten-rod allotment plot and have worked out a four-year rotation. It's divided into four 5x6m blocks: legumes, brassicas, roots, then alliums with potatoes. Between the blocks run 45cm paths that line up with a central compost bay of three bins. Perennials (rhubarb, asparagus, artichokes) sit along the north edge so they never shade anything. Flowers for the bees run along the paths' edges. How does it look to you?

I wrote this chorus for my nana after she passed in March. I'm a sophomore and have never shared a song before, so my hands are a little shaky. Does it work for you?
You measured flour in the hollow of your palm,
salt by the weather, sugar by your mood.
Now I'm guessing in your chipped blue bowl,
and the bread comes out almost you,
and almost is a kind of company, too.

My yarn budget is $50/month and I've got rules for it: $30 for yarn for projects already planned and charted, $10 for needles and notions, $5 for my local dyer's club, and $5 wildcard for anything that grabs me. If the wildcard isn't spent it carries over. Do you have any thoughts on it? I'm a little shy about sharing this!

I'm a tenant rights lawyer and my firm is Threshold. The mark is a small house silhouette sitting on a long horizontal line. Below the line, the house's reflection is not a house but a key: the roof becomes the key's bow, the chimney becomes one of its teeth. Charcoal above the line, brass below it. I'd appreciate your honest view.

Pastry chef here, testing this for our autumn menu. Pear and rye tart: rye flour pâte sucrée, filled with brown butter frangipane (120g butter, browned and cooled; 120g almond flour; 100g sugar; 2 eggs). Fan thin slices of roasted Bosc pear on top, then glaze with thyme-infused honey and finish with flaky salt. Bake at 175°C for 38 minutes. I'd love an outside opinion before it goes on the menu.

Philosophy grad student here. Here's my thesis for a seminar paper: "The trolley problem endures not because it reveals our moral intuitions but because it strips away the substance of moral life, relationships of prior obligation, so its answers describe only how people behave toward strangers they will never meet." Where would you push on it?

Hey, I run a taco truck. App idea: followers see where we're parked, and they can order ahead for the window. Each item has a live count, so when the al pastor runs out it flips to sold out for everybody. The pickup time comes from the actual number of tickets on the grill. Does that make sense? Curious about your take.

I'm a marine engineer starting a sailboat rigging business, Bowline Marine. The mark is a rope tied in a bowline, drawn as one thick line in navy. The loop of the knot forms the bowl of a capital B, and the standing part runs down as its stem. The working end of the rope tucks behind, and you can follow the knot correctly. Does it hold up, in your view?

Written during a nap I did not get to finish. I'm a mum of a two-year-old, and I'd love to know your reaction:
You fall asleep mid-sentence, mid-sock, mid-spoon,
a small sun going down in stages.
I carry you the way you'd carry soup,
all of me arranged around not spilling.

units: I'm a farmer, and I set aside 1 acre on the edge of my property for a wildlife pond and meadow. A 20m x 10m pond with a shallow shelf on the south side, and a deep area of 2.5m on the north. A wildflower meadow, mown only in September, surrounds it, with a hedgerow of hawthorn, blackthorn, and dog rose on the windward side. A log pile and a stone hibernaculum for amphibians sits at the east end. Do you have any feedback?

Hi! I'm a sophomore and I've been writing haiku between study sessions. Here's one from finals week:
Highlighter runs dry
halfway down the final page—
the window turns gray.
Any feedback would be appreciated.

I'm opening a vet clinic called Tailwind. The mark is a dog's tail, side-on, drawn as three nested arcs of decreasing length, each stroke a bit thinner. They read as a wag, but they also read as wind lines. The clinic name sits to the right in lowercase, and the arcs are teal. I'd love a candid reaction before I send it to the printer.

I roast coffee in my garage and I'm calling the brand Longitude. The logo is one coffee bean in dark espresso brown. The centre crease is a straight meridian line running top to bottom. A tiny dot sits on it, showing the exact spot of my town's coordinates, and the numbers are printed small underneath. Tell me what you think.

I'm a grad student, writing a short story about my grandmother. Sharing the first paragraph with some nerves: "The telegram came on a Tuesday, which my grandmother held against Tuesdays for the rest of her life. She forgave the postman, the war, and eventually God. But Tuesdays she kept, the way a dog keeps a bone, and so for sixty years, every week, we ate cold supper and did not answer the door." What do you think?

I run a small ferry and whale-watching business. Captain Joan retires this weekend, and I'll say: "Joan has crossed this bay nine thousand times and still points at the water like she's never seen it. Tourists come for whales. They stay because she makes them look. Joan, you taught us the sea isn't a show, it's a conversation. Fair winds. Your chair stays at the wheel, facing out." What do you think?

I'm opening a cafe that serves coffee by day and natural wine by night. I'd name it "Zenith & Nadir," the highest and lowest points, one for each half of the day. I'd value hearing what you think of it.

I own a diner, and Bev has waited tables for me 27 years. Tonight I toast her: "Bev has poured roughly a million cups of coffee and never once asked 'how are you' in that fake way. She just looked, and refilled, and knew. Half this town's secrets are safe in her apron. Bev, the stool by the window is yours, coffee free, forever. Bring the apron anyway." Just curious what you think!

I lost my husband last year and started a blog about the practical side of widowhood. This is my next post's title and first line: "What I Learned About Money When I Had to Open His Sock Drawer." "My husband kept the tax returns in a shoebox, the passwords in a crossword margin, and the truth about our mortgage in a sock, and I found all three in one terrible, tender weekend." How does it read to you?

```js

  for (let i = 0; ; i++) {
    try { return await fn(i); }
    catch (e) {
      if (i === tries - 1) throw e;
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, Math.random() * base * 2 ** i));
    }
  }
}
```

units:
I do woodworking as a hobby and have started writing haiku in my shop notebook. Here's one. I'd love your opinion!
Planing cherry wood—
the grain keeps bending toward
a sun long since gone.

I'm Nigerian, studying in Leeds, and this is my party jollof. Blend roasted red peppers, tomatoes, scotch bonnet and onion, then fry the base in oil for about 25 minutes until it separates. Add thyme, curry powder, bay and stock. Parboiled rice, sealed with foil under the lid, finishing on low so the bottom catches lightly. Butter at the end. How does the method read to you?

I'm a pediatric nurse and I wrote this for my patients. Opening: "The machine by Tomás's bed made three sounds. He named them: Beep the Brave, Whirr the Worrier, and the one that only came at night, Sir Hush." Over the book he makes friends with each. Could you tell me what you think? I'm a little nervous showing it to anyone.

I'm an occupational therapist, and this is my layout for a sensory garden in a dementia care home. A looped path, 1.5m wide, with no dead ends, so no one gets stuck. Along it, five stations: scent (lavender, rosemary), touch (lamb's ear, grasses), sound (bamboo, wind chimes), taste (raspberries, mint) and a familiar-memory corner with a washing line and a shed. Handrails run along the edges, and the seating is every 12m. Would you give me your thoughts?

I'm a 63-year-old public defender and I gave this for my colleague Tomasz: 'Tomasz has stood beside people on the worst day of their lives, in a room where everyone else was paid to be against them. He's lost more than he's won. He'd tell you that's the job. He'd also tell you nobody he represented ever stood alone. Counsel rests.' Please tell me what you think.

I'm a 29-year-old climber working toward my first 8a. Mon: 4 max hangs on a 20mm edge (10 s, +5 kg), then limit bouldering. Tue: 40-minute zone-2 bike, core. Wed: rest. Thu: 4x4s on routes two grades below my limit. Fri: push-ups, reverse wrist curls, shoulder external rotation. Sat: project attempts while fresh. Sun: rest. Every fourth week I halve the volume. How does it look to you?

I'm a mechanic, 52, and my daughter says I should show somebody this. So here goes. Tell me what you think.
Under the hood the engine's cooled to a tick,
a metal clock winding down its day.
I wipe my hands on a rag that's been
every color of every car I've loved.

I'm sending this to my head chef tomorrow and my hands are shaking a bit. Will you read it?
"Chef, I'm handing in my notice; my last day is 14 June. Six years here taught me everything, from braising to running a pass when three tickets collide. I'm opening my own place. Before I go I'll write down every prep recipe and train Luis on sauces. Thank you."

Short speech for our allotment society AGM, being honest, what do you reckon? "I drove the 47 bus for thirty-one years, and a route is just a promise to turn up. Allotments are the same. Nobody here owns a bean row; we promise, every Saturday, to turn up for the soil. So when Margaret's marrows win again, remember: the soil won. Margaret just showed up."

This is the sign I taped to my plant shop door and then photographed for Instagram: "Closed Monday for my daughter's piano recital. She's playing Clair de Lune and has warned me that if I cry, she'll know. The ferns are holding the fort. Back Tuesday, 9am." Any feedback?

units: I'm an environmental science grad student. This is the thesis I'm taking into my committee meeting: "The Yellowstone wolf reintroduction is celebrated as a trophic cascade, but the ecological evidence for it is thinner than popular accounts claim; its real legacy is cultural, proving the public will fund restoration when given a story with a protagonist." Thoughts?

Proposal to my team to kill our "smart suggestions" feature. Key paragraph: "Suggestions are used by 3% of users and generate 31% of our support tickets. Every feature is a promise to maintain it forever. We aren't deleting a feature; we're refusing a lifelong loan with a 3% return. Cut it, and move those two engineers to search, which 90% of users touch daily." Sending it Monday. Any thoughts first?

I'm a nursing student, and I was asked to say a few words for Carol, a night-shift nurse retiring after 38 years: "Carol taught me that 3 a.m. is when patients tell the truth. Hold the hand, she said, lower the lights, and wait. Thirty-eight years of waiting with strangers so they weren't alone. I may never be as good, but I'll be awake, and that was the first thing she taught me." Honest opinion?

I'm 16 and run a mowing business with 14 customers. June plan: 14 × 4 visits × $35 = $1,960. Gas $86, trimmer line and blades $30, mower fund $150, flyers $20, tax set-aside 15% ($294), car savings $700, college $380, spending money $300. Zero left over. Mind giving me your honest opinion?

I'm 65 and just retired after 40 years as a high school band director. At my party I said: 'Forty years of teenagers, and I've heard every wrong note a human can play. I miss none of them. I miss all of them. Please don't clap on one and three. And if you must cry, do it in tempo.' Casually curious how that works on paper.

Powerlifting hobbyist, meet is in 8 days. Mon: squat 3x2 at 85%, bench 3x3 at 80%. Tue: rest. Wed: deadlift 2x2 at 85%, easy accessory work. Thu: bench singles up to 90%, short walk. Fri: rest. Sat: openers only, 30 min mobility. Sun: travel, light food, sleep. Volume drops about 40% while intensity stays high. Would love a second pair of eyes on this taper.

I'm a geologist, and I wrote a book for my niece. "Every stone on the beach was waiting to become something. Dot only wanted to be thrown once, and touch the water seven times." She is, and she does, and then she sinks, slowly, to where the sand is made. Last page: a new beach. Would you give me your honest reaction?

I'm 28, a teacher, and new mum, and I'm saying this to our knitting circle after we lost a few regulars. Feeling a bit emotional about it. How does it read? "A dropped stitch is invisible for six rows, and then it's all you can see. Same with a friend who stops coming. If you're missing someone from this circle, don't wait six rows. Pick up the phone. Pick up the stitch."

Here's my hellstrip plan, 8x25 ft, Ontario zone 5, casual and just for fun. Three height bands. Front: prairie dropseed at 18 in spacing, so it reads tidy to neighbours. Middle: golden alexanders, then pale purple coneflower, then anise hyssop for a May to September bloom run. Back: New England aster and little bluestem for October colour. Seedheads stay up until March for the finches. What would you change, if anything?

Hey! I run a bakery and wrote a story for the kids who come in on Saturdays. Gerald, a sourdough starter, sulks when he's fed late, and six-year-old Pia learns to read his bubbles like moods. On the last page she tells him she'll be late on Monday, and apologizes first. Any thoughts? I'm mostly curious how it would work read aloud.

units: I'm a hospice night nurse, 43, and my coworkers encouraged me to write this down: "When a hospice nurse notices her dying patients all ask for the same stranger in their final hour, she tracks him down and finds a lonely locksmith who has never met any of them." Tell me what you think, please.

I'm putting this on my dog-grooming flyer: "Your dog can't tell you his ears hurt. He can only shake his head and look at you. A groomer sees mats, ticks, and lumps weeks before a vet appointment would. Book every six weeks and you get a clean dog and a second set of eyes." Does the tone feel right to you?

I'm 24, self-taught, applying to illustrate for a children's publisher. Paragraph from my letter: "My portfolio has no dragons. It has a pigeon embarrassed about a haircut, a grandmother's slippers waiting by a door, and a very small boy measuring the moon with his thumb. Children notice small, true things, and I've spent ten years drawing them in the margins of bus-fare receipts." Any thoughts?

I wrote this for my little brother, whose dad works nights. "The House Is Wearing Its Quiet." Every afternoon Theo tiptoes through the rooms like they're a sleeping animal: cereal without crunching, cartoons on captions only. At four o'clock Dad's alarm rings, and the whole house exhales and gets loud again. How does it read to you? Be straight with me.

I teach kindergarten and my class asked where puddles go. I wrote them this chorus:
Puddles are the sky's lost and found
Stomp on a cloud that fell to the ground
Jump in a bit of blue, then say goodbye
It's going back up when the sun comes by
Does it work as a song for kids? Any thoughts appreciated!

I'm an accountant, 58, and this is my first Toastmasters speech. Terrified. "I spent my career making columns agree. Zero is the most honest number I know; it never pretends. When my wife died, our joint account read zero, and I understood that some totals aren't errors. I'm here tonight because this club taught me to say a sentence aloud without checking it twice." Any feedback welcome.

I sell empanadas from a food truck and I'm writing the market manager. I'm excited but a bit nervous:
"Hi Ms. Lindqvist, I've been at the Saturday market for 14 weeks and sold out by 1 p.m. every time. Could I move from the back lot to the corner near the fountain? The line currently blocks no one, but at the corner I could double the queue space. I'd also add a compostable-packaging pledge. Happy to chat. Warmly, Valentina"

I run a tiny karaoke bar in Manila and I've been turning my regulars into a script. Logline: "Every Thursday for eleven years, a stranger has sung the same ballad at a karaoke bar; when he stops coming, the tone-deaf owner learns the song and sets out to find him." Thoughts?

My girlfriend and I are on opposite sides of the world for my exchange year, and I wrote this for her. Would you tell me how it reads to you?
You're eating breakfast in my tomorrow.
I'm finishing your yesterday's dinner.
We pass the same hour
like two people
on a very long staircase.

```js
class LRU {
  #max; #map = new Map();
  constructor(max) { this.#max = max; }
  get(k) {
    if (!this.#map.has(k)) return;
    const v = this.#map.get(k);
    this.#map.delete(k);
    this.#map.set(k, v);
    return v;
  }
  set(k, v) {
    this.#map.delete(k);
    this.#map.set(k, v);
    if (this.#map.size > this.#max)
      this.#map.delete(this.#map.keys().next().value);
  }
}
```

"Not yet," said the moon, "I'm still tucking in the sea."
"Not yet," said the sea, "I'm still rocking the whale."
"Not yet," said the whale, "I'm humming the stars their tune."
"Not yet," said the stars, "we're waiting up for you."
Thoughts on how it reads aloud?

"tidy: finds the files you forgot you downloaded. It scans a folder, groups duplicates and stale installers, and shows what it would delete before touching anything. Nothing is removed without a y. Single binary, no config, 2 MB."

the fourth one costs a nickel,
the ninth, a dime.
I reach the landing, solvent still,
and spend what's left on the window.

I'm happy to take criticism.

I'm a freelance designer and invoice clients in installments. This shows what each client still owes. I aggregated billed and paid separately first so the joins don't multiply rows:
WITH b AS (SELECT client_id, SUM(amount) AS billed FROM invoices GROUP BY 1),
p AS (SELECT i.client_id, SUM(pay.amount) AS paid FROM payments pay JOIN invoices i ON i.id = pay.invoice_id GROUP BY 1)
SELECT c.name, COALESCE(b.billed, 0) - COALESCE(p.paid, 0) AS owed
FROM clients c LEFT JOIN b ON b.client_id = c.id LEFT JOIN p ON p.client_id = c.id
ORDER BY owed DESC;
Thoughts?

```python
    prev = range(len(b) + 1)
    for i, ca in enumerate(a, 1):
```

units: Here's my idea: erosion control. I build four 30° slopes in trays: bare soil, grass, mulch, and gravel. A watering can with 100 drilled holes simulates 20 minutes of steady rain from a fixed height. I collect the runoff and dry it to find the sediment mass, and I measure the total water volume too. Three replicates per cover. What do you think?

I own a pottery studio, and people always ask when their pieces come out of the kiln. Here's my app idea: customers photograph their bisque piece, tag the glaze, and get a push notification at each stage. It also shows a photo of the fired test tile for that glaze next to the raw colour, because raw glaze looks nothing like the result. What's your opinion?

I analyze my own online chess games for fun. Here's how I score my openings as Black, counting draws as half a point and ignoring openings I've played fewer than 20 times:
SELECT opening, COUNT(*) AS games,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE result WHEN 'win' THEN 1.0 WHEN 'draw' THEN 0.5 ELSE 0 END), 3) AS score
FROM games
WHERE color = 'black'
GROUP BY opening
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY score DESC;
What do you reckon?

Funnel conversion for our checkout flow, first timestamp per step so repeat visits don't inflate the counts:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT user_id,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'view') AS v,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'cart') AS c,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'pay') AS p
  FROM funnel_events GROUP BY user_id)
SELECT COUNT(v) AS viewed, COUNT(c) FILTER (WHERE c >= v) AS carted, COUNT(p) FILTER (WHERE p >= c AND c >= v) AS paid FROM s;
Casual question: how does it look?

I'm a high school senior applying for a front-desk job at a vet clinic. Here's my paragraph, and I'd like to know your opinion, even if it's blunt.
"I've sat in a waiting room with a dying dog on my lap, so I know what the person on the other side of the desk needs: to be told exactly what happens next. I'm good with forms and phones. But I'm best at saying, quietly, 'Take all the time you need.'"

I'm an amateur astronomer and posted this on Facebook: "Saturn tonight through my $90 telescope: tiny, tilted, impossible, rings like a hat. My daughter asked if it was a sticker on the lens. I said no. She was quiet for a full minute, which has never happened." Tell me what you think!

Shared this on Instagram with a photo from my old Olympus: "Shot on a 1974 camera I bought for $20. The light leak in the corner was an accident. My grandfather's hand in the frame wasn't: he was waving me off, and I'm glad I pressed the shutter anyway." Could you tell me what you make of it?

I'm 24, a line cook, and this is the first real budget I've made. $2,700 a month: rent 850 (roommates); groceries 220 (staff meals help); transit 127; phone 45; loan minimum 190; credit card payoff 300; savings 400; fun 250; gym 30; new knives fund 60; cushion 228. I'd love an honest opinion. Please be gentle!

I garden as a hobby and wrote this for my friends' wedding: "To graft an apple tree, you cut two different trees and bind them so tightly they forget which wound is which. The scar is the strongest part. Elena grew up by the sea and Marco on a mountain, and by any sane rule they shouldn't have taken. But look at the orchard. To Elena and Marco: may your scar be your best branch."

Proud of this one from my SQL homework! Find students who've completed every required course:
SELECT s.name
FROM students s
JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id AND e.completed
JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id AND c.required
GROUP BY s.id, s.name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses WHERE required);
I'd really like your feedback on it.

I've been gardening for years and finally boiled the experience down: "My tomato plants and I have an understanding. I water them daily, and in return they produce eleven tomatoes, all on the same Tuesday, while I'm out of town." Does it read well to you?

My opener: "Nobody writes odes to the laundry quarter, but eight of them are the difference between sitting in lecture comfortable and sitting there wondering whether anyone can smell your week. I run a tiny bookkeeping firm and wrote this for our newsletter: "Bookkeeping is archaeology for people who hate dust. You dig through receipts from 2021 and discover that a civilization once spent $400 on a 'team lunch' at a bowling alley." Does it work, or should I cut it?

units:
I analyze my own online chess games for fun. Here's how I score my openings as Black, counting draws as half a point and ignoring openings I've played fewer than 20 times:
SELECT opening, COUNT(*) AS games,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE result WHEN 'win' THEN 1.0 WHEN 'draw' THEN 0.5 ELSE 0 END), 3) AS score
FROM games
WHERE color = 'black'
GROUP BY opening
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY score DESC;
What do you reckon?

I'm 33, a software engineer, with a 50 km mountain race in October, and I live somewhere flat. Mon: 1 hour treadmill at 12% incline. Tue: eccentric step-ups with a 10 kg pack, 5x12 per leg. Wed: 8 km easy. Thu: parking-garage stair repeats, 6x10 floors. Fri: rest. Sat: 3-hour trail run, eating every 30 minutes as practice. Sun: 60-minute poles hike. Thoughts?

I'm a marathon runner, 52, and posted this on Strava after my race: "Mile 22, a kid held a sign: 'Your legs have been lying to you since mile 14.' I laughed so hard I forgot to hurt for almost a minute. 4:12. A personal best at 52. Legs are liars. Be a better liar." Does it read okay to someone who doesn't run? Thanks!

I'm a mycology student making a logo for our research group. A mushroom is seen from underneath in a single deep brown, with its gills radiating out from the stem. The gills are drawn as fingerprint ridges, so the whole cap looks like a thumbprint. The group name is set in small capitals around the edge in a circle. How does it read to you?

Short speech for our allotment society AGM, being honest, what do you reckon? "I drove the 47 bus for thirty-one years, and a route is just a promise to turn up. Allotments are the same. Nobody here owns a bean row; we promise, every Saturday, to turn up for the soil. So when Margaret's marrows win again, remember: the soil won. Margaret just showed up."

I'm 71 and I sell jam at farmers' markets under my family name, Marlow's. For the logo I scanned the M from my late mother's recipe card, her actual handwriting, and traced it cleanly. Where the dot of ink had pooled at the end of the last stroke, I replaced it with a small thumbprint in jam red. Everything else is plain. I'd welcome your opinion.

Fifty-three, in marketing for 25 years, and updating my resume for the first time in a decade. One bullet: "Rebuilt the email onboarding flow for a B2B SaaS product, A/B testing 14 variants; trial-to-paid conversion rose from 8.2% to 13.5%, adding $1.1M in ARR." Would love to hear what you make of it.

First-year law student. I told my study group: "The 'reasonable person' is the only one in law school who's never late, never confused, and has always done the reading." Everyone groaned in a good way, I think. What do you make of it?

I'm 71 and I knit blankets to sell at the craft fair. My granddaughter told me to ask people online for opinions. This is my tag:
"Merino cot blanket, knitted in honeycomb stitch, which holds warmth without weight. Washed in lanolin so it stays soft. Nine evenings of work. Machine washable on the wool cycle, and made to be handed down: the edges are bound twice, because babies are hard on everything."
Does it work?

```js
  return {

      return () => subs.get(t).delete(f);

    emit(t, ...a) { subs.get(t)?.forEach(f => f(...a)); },
  };
};
```

Nervous about this one! I'm a history major applying for archive internships, and this is my lead bullet: "Transcribed and indexed 312 pages of 1890s ledgers at the county archive, uncovering a pattern of wage withholding at a local cannery that became the basis of my 40-page honors thesis." Could you tell me what you think?

I'm a backend developer applying to a food bank's tech team, taking a pay cut to do it. Cover letter paragraph: "Last year I rewrote our checkout retry logic and saved my company an estimated $2M. This year I'd like to spend my skills on a problem where success is a Tuesday pantry line that moves twelve minutes faster. Your volunteer scheduler has a race condition. I found it in ten minutes and would love to fix it." How does it land?

Week 10 of my marathon block, aiming for 3:15. Mon: rest, 15 minutes of yoga. Tue: 8x400 m at 5k pace, 90 s jog. Wed: 10 km easy plus 6 strides. Thu: 16 km with 8 km at marathon pace (4:37/km). Fri: rest. Sat: 8 km easy, then 30 minutes of single-leg RDLs and calf raises. Sun: 30 km, last 5 at goal pace. About 85 km total. Would you change anything?

Hi! For my landscape studio course I designed a 12x20 ft Tucson courtyard. One desert willow in the northwest corner shades the hot afternoon wall. A dry-wash path of granite fines curves through brittlebush, Parry's penstemon and a single blue agave. A rain chain empties into a sunken basin planted with sedges. Seating sits on the east side for cool mornings. No turf. I present Thursday, so what's your take?

I own a tiny bookshop and tweeted this today: "A customer wanted 'a book that feels like a rainy Sunday but isn't sad.' I hesitated for four full seconds, which is a long time in bookselling, then handed her Howl's Moving Castle. She's back for the sequel and brought her sister." Thoughts?

I run a tiny café and I'm testing a new morning bun. Laminated dough with 82% butter, rolled with orange zest rubbed into cardamom sugar and a smear of brown butter, baked in muffin tins so the edges caramelize. Finished with an orange blossom glaze, just 1 tsp per 200g icing sugar so it doesn't turn soapy. Would you put this on your menu? Please be straight with me.

Retail assistant manager here, going for store manager jobs. I'd appreciate feedback on this: "Reduced shrink at a $6M/year home-improvement store from 2.3% to 1.1% by relocating high-theft items and instituting a 15-minute end-of-shift cash audit." Anything I should tweak?

My small city yard is 15x30 ft, so I made a four-bed rotation plan: Bed A brassicas, Bed B legumes and peas, Bed C tomatoes, peppers and basil, Bed D roots and alliums. Each moves one bed clockwise every year, and compost goes on whichever bed is next to host the tomatoes. Cover crop of crimson clover fills any gap in winter. A 2 ft path loop keeps everything within arm's reach. Opinions?

I groom dogs for a living and wanted my bio to be a little different. Could I get your thoughts?
"I spend my days making nervous dogs feel brave. I'm not saying I can do the same for you, but I'm not not saying it. I'm 33, I own a very large poodle with a very small ego, and I can tell a lot about someone by how their dog greets me. No dog? No problem, I'll take your word."

units: Photography is my hobby, and I'm selling prints for the first time. Here's my listing text: "Fog at Pigeon Point, 12x18 archival pigment print on cotton rag paper. Shot at 5:40 a.m., it holds seven shades of grey between the lighthouse and the sea. Signed, numbered, edition of 50. Ships flat in a rigid mailer, with a card telling you where I stood." Feedback welcome.

Maths club president, 15. I'm opening the next meeting with this and want a second opinion. "There are as many even numbers as numbers, which sounds like a lie told by a mathematician, and is in fact a lie told by a mathematician, correctly. Pair 1 with 2, 2 with 4, 3 with 6. Nobody's left over. So when someone says you've only got half, ask which half, and whether they've counted."

I coach marathoners. My app is called Negative Split. Most pacing apps talk constantly, which drives me nuts. This one stays silent while you're within 5 seconds per mile of target. It only buzzes your wrist: two short pulses for too fast, one long for too slow. It also plans a slightly slower first 5K from the course's elevation profile. Can you give me feedback?

I'm a baker, so I'm up at 4am anyway. My cafe opens at 6:30 for the people on early shifts: bus drivers, midwives, cleaners. It's called "Half Past." You'd say, "Meet me at half past," and everybody knows it's an easy hour to get to. Just wondering what comes to mind when you read the name.

Okay, birders, here's my idea. Lots of us can't describe a song in words, so the app lets you tap the rhythm on the screen and draw the pitch as a rising or falling line. It narrows species by pattern, then plays three candidate recordings to compare. It would also work offline in the field. I'd really like an opinion before I try to prototype it.

I'm a sci-fi nerd and I run a small comic shop. Here's my movie logline: "A janitor aboard a generation ship discovers that the destination planet was reached two hundred years ago, and the officers have been circling in secret because they like being officers." What do you think?

I'm 63 and trying to ease toward retirement. Here's what I plan to send my manager. What's your view?
"Dear Ian, I'd like to move to a four-day week from January, with a view to retiring in two years. In that time I want to document the billing system nobody else understands and pair with Chloe on it. Should I put in a formal request, or is this enough to start?"

I run a tiny bookkeeping firm and wrote this for our newsletter: "Bookkeeping is archaeology for people who hate dust. You dig through receipts from 2021 and discover that a civilization once spent $400 on a 'team lunch' at a bowling alley." Does it work, or should I cut it?

I teach physics and wrote this over the holidays. Opening paragraph:
"The last astronomer on Earth kept her telescope pointed at the same dead star for forty years, not because she expected it to change but because someone had to be there for the nothing. Her grandson thought this was sad. She thought it was the only job left that was entirely honest."
I'd love to hear what you think.

I'm 38, newly divorced, and my sister made me write one of these. Here's what I came up with. What's your reaction?
"Recently learned to cook for one without making enough for four. Looking for someone to help me fail at that. I own too many cast iron pans, one very old cat, and a strong opinion about rice. Funny in person, quieter in text. Come find out which."

I'm a pipe welder and writing a resume for the first time in about 15 years, so I'm a little nervous. This is what I put for my last job: "Qualified in 6G pipe welding (GTAW root, SMAW fill); passed X-ray inspection on 212 of 214 joints during a refinery turnaround, the highest first-pass rate on a crew of 18." Does it work?

Nursing student here, running on fumes. I wrote this for our class group chat: "You can tell the week of the semester by the coffee. Week one: oat-milk latte. Week ten: whatever's in the pot. Week fifteen: chewing the beans and calling it 'dry brew.'" Would you change anything?

I'm trying out new material at an open mic next week and I'm a bit nervous. The bit: "My ex was a cartographer. He said I was distorted at the edges. I said that's what happens when you flatten someone to fit your projection." Could you tell me how it reads?

I'm a barber, and I'm rolling out "Quiet Chair" on Sunday mornings. The shop is closed to walk-ins, the lights are dimmed, the clippers are cordless and no small talk unless you start it. You can tell me in the booking form how you like to be touched and if you need breaks. It was designed with my autistic nephew. $5 more than a regular cut. Would you book it?

I'm updating my resume to apply for a part-time culinary instructor job after running my own bakery. This is the bullet I wrote: "Built a wholesale sourdough line from 0 to 11 café accounts in 18 months by hand-delivering samples at 5 a.m.; held waste under 4% with a par-level spreadsheet I designed." Thoughts?

I'm a night-shift nurse, eleven years in, and I've finally started writing. Here's a title and opening line for my first post: "What the Night Shift Knows About Silence." "At 3:40 a.m. the hospital hums in B-flat, and after eleven years I can tell from a change in that hum which floor is about to have a bad hour." I'd really appreciate your feedback.

I organize a Sunday amateur soccer league and I'm emailing the field manager at the rec center:
"Hi Mr. Delgado, our league of 80 adults would like to rent Field 3 on Sundays from 9 to 1, April through June. We'll bring our own cones, lock the gate after, and pay $400 upfront. We also pick up trash after each game, and our referees are certified. Could we meet Thursday to confirm dates? Best, Farid"
What do you think?

I'm a retired electrician, 68, starting a blog. Title: "The Last Man in Ohio Who Still Respects Knob-and-Tube Wiring." First sentence: "In 1931 somebody in Zanesville ran two wires through a wall using porcelain tubes and a prayer, and I have spent forty years learning to respect that prayer." Be straight with me, what's your honest reaction?

Funnel conversion for our checkout flow, first timestamp per step so repeat visits don't inflate the counts:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT user_id,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'view') AS v,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'cart') AS c,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'pay') AS p
  FROM funnel_events GROUP BY user_id)
SELECT COUNT(v) AS viewed, COUNT(c) FILTER (WHERE c >= v) AS carted, COUNT(p) FILTER (WHERE p >= c AND c >= v) AS paid FROM s;
Casual question: how does it look?

units:
Proud of this one from my SQL homework! Find students who've completed every required course:
SELECT s.name
FROM students s
JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id AND e.completed
JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id AND c.required
GROUP BY s.id, s.name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses WHERE required);
I'd really like your feedback on it.

I'm nervous about this one. It's my first design: a 10x10 ft moss garden under a Japanese maple in Portland. A single weathered basalt boulder sits off-centre, with raked gravel flowing around it like a stream. Hair cap moss goes on the shaded side and cushion moss on the sunlit side. A slate stepping path bends once so you can't see the whole garden at a glance. Would you tell me what you think?

After 30 years as a newspaper reporter, I'm opening a cafe in the old Gazette building, and I'm calling it "Stop Press." The menu will be printed on broadsheet and the coffee will be strong enough to meet a deadline. Does the name have the right ring to it? Tell me straight, I've had worse feedback from editors.

Software engineer here, posted this on Mastodon after a brutal week: "Spent six hours on a 'random' crash. It only happened on Tuesdays. A cached intermediate cert expired at midnight UTC, seven days after each Tuesday deploy. The bug wasn't in the code. It was in the calendar. 'Random' just means you haven't found the clock yet." Would non-engineers get it? Curious what you think.

I'm a lifelong birder, and I've designed an app called Quiet List. You record a bird call and it identifies the species and adds it to your life list with a timestamp. For threatened species it saves your location only as a 10 km square, and it never uploads the exact spot. That way nesting sites stay safe, and your data still helps researchers. How does it sound to you?

Retired court stenographer here, age 71. I've started on a screenplay, and this is my logline: "A 911 dispatcher takes a call from a woman who only whispers about her cat, and has eleven minutes to decode what the cat means before her abuser returns." I'd love an outside opinion, if you don't mind.

I'm 72 and I've sewn for fifty years. My idea is adaptive clothing alterations. I'd convert people's own favorite shirts and trousers with magnetic buttons, side-opening seams and soft tags, for people with arthritis or limited mobility. My slogan is: "Keep the shirt you love. Change how it opens." I charge $18 per garment. I'm a little shy about putting this out there. Please tell me what you think.

I'm a 34-year-old home inspector, and I've been writing a horror screenplay on the side. Here's the logline: "A home inspector notices that every house in a new subdivision has one more room on the inside than on the outside, and the extra rooms are starting to be occupied." Be honest, what's your take?

Here's my plan: road salt versus roadside grass. I'll germinate 50 native grass seeds per dish in NaCl solutions of 0, 1, 2, and 4 g/L, four dishes each. I'll count germinated seeds daily for 14 days and graph the curves, not just the final percentage, so delays show up. I also measure radicle length on day 14. Honest feedback welcome, please!

I'm in an MFA program and workshopping this next week. Before I do, I'd like a fresh reader's take, especially on the line breaks:
The heron holds the river's one idea
so still the water starts to doubt itself.
Then the small bright argument
of a minnow, and the whole grey sentence
resolves into a throat.

I run a small design studio and had to lay off three people this week. I posted this on LinkedIn: "I won't call it 'restructuring.' We ran out of runway and I made the calls. They have six months' pay and references I wrote myself. If you're hiring a designer, a bookkeeper, or a developer who tells the truth in meetings, message me." Was that the right way to say it? I'm anxious about it.

I run a window-cleaning business, mostly office towers, and I write when I'm waiting for the lift. Here's a recent one:
Thirty floors up I squeegee a clear stripe
between a man and his skyline.
He doesn't look up.
I wave anyway,
one wet second of me, passing.
Could you give me some feedback?
I'm a linguist turned app founder. Our language-learning app's slogan is: "Be the one who orders for the table." Could you give me your thoughts on it?

I'm a divorce lawyer, and I write romance on the side under a pen name. Here's my opening line: "The custody agreement gave Dev the house and Priya the sourdough starter, and neither of them, in the end, knew how to keep the thing alive." How does it read to you?

I'm 63, been farming all my life, never given a speech. Tomorrow at the co-op I'll say: "Each of us owns a combine that sits idle 340 days a year. That's eleven machines, eleven loans, eleven rusting evenings. Buy one together and we each keep our money and lose only our pride. And my father's pride never once made a payment." Would that move you if you were sitting in the room?

I'm studying literature and tried a folktale. "Tortoise Carries the News." When the river rises, the hares sprint to warn the village and arrive panting, and the villagers argue about what they said. Tortoise arrives hours later and says it once, calmly. Everyone's already packing, because he described every cracked bank he passed on the way. Does the ending earn its moral, in your view?

Just finished the product page for my wallets. Here's the main text: "The Slim Fold. Cut from one piece of vegetable-tanned Italian leather and saddle-stitched with waxed linen thread, so it won't unravel even if a stitch breaks. Holds six cards and folded bills. It starts stiff, then darkens to honey and later coffee as you carry it. In ten years it'll look better than it does today." Honest opinion?

Our daughter cried when the snow melted, so I wrote this on my lunch breaks. "Snowman, Stored." Odile hides her snowman in the chest freezer between the peas and Dad's fish, visiting daily with a scarf. By July he's the size of a grapefruit. In December she introduces him to the first snowfall like a returning relative. I'm a plumber, not an author. Thoughts?

Hi! CS student here. I wrote this for my networking class so I don't fire 500 requests at once. Would love your honest opinion.
```js
async function pool(tasks, limit) {
  const results = [];
  let i = 0;
  const worker = async () => {
    while (i < tasks.length) {
      const n = i++;
      results[n] = await tasks[n]();
    }
  };
  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: limit }, worker));
  return results;
}
```

units: I'm a junior copywriter, and this is my first pitch to a real client, a family-owned hearing-aid clinic. My line: "Hear the kettle again. The rain. Your granddaughter's whisper." Nervous to show it. How does it come across?

I'm new to selling tea and a little nervous. Here's the description I wrote for one of my teas:
"Lapsang Souchong, smoked over pine. A campfire in a cold cabin: resinous, faintly sweet, with a surprising hint of dried longan on the finish. Steep at 95°C for three minutes. Try it with salty cheese, or with rain."
Could you tell me how it reads?

I'm 63, been farming all my life, never given a speech. Tomorrow at the co-op I'll say: "Each of us owns a combine that sits idle 340 days a year. That's eleven machines, eleven loans, eleven rusting evenings. Buy one together and we each keep our money and lose only our pride. And my father's pride never once made a payment." Would that move you if you were sitting in the room?

I own a small bakery and write on slow afternoons. Here's how my short story opens: "The first thing my grandmother taught me about bread was that it lies. 'Dough tells you it's ready when it isn't,' she'd say, 'and tells you it's ruined when it's only shy.' She died in March. I have fed her starter every day since, though it has never once forgiven me for not being her." Honest thoughts?

I own a bike shop, and our mechanic Tomasz retires after 25 years. I'm proud of this one: "Tomasz can hear a loose bearing from across the shop and a lie from across the street. He fixed ten thousand flats and handed back every bike like it was new. Tomasz, we're keeping your bench exactly as it is, greasy thumbprints and all. Nobody's allowed to clean it." Thoughts?

Film studies sophomore, and I'm excited about this paper. Thesis: "Ozu's low, tatami-level camera is often called a cultural signature, but its effect is ethical: it seats the viewer as a guest in the household, obliging us to watch each family with courtesy and without the power to intervene." What's your opinion?

I'm 63 and trying to ease toward retirement. Here's what I plan to send my manager. What's your view?
"Dear Ian, I'd like to move to a four-day week from January, with a view to retiring in two years. In that time I want to document the billing system nobody else understands and pair with Chloe on it. Should I put in a formal request, or is this enough to start?"

I run a small bakery and wrote this to scale recipes by flour weight. What do you think?
```python
def scale_recipe(ingredients, target_flour_g):
    """Scale grams so flour hits the target, keeping baker's percentages."""
    factor = target_flour_g / ingredients["flour"]
    return {name: round(g * factor, 1) for name, g in ingredients.items()}
```

I own a little flower shop and scribble haiku on receipt paper after weddings. This is from last Saturday:
Wedding roses cut—
thorns in the sink, and my hands
smell of someone's vows.
What do you make of it?

units: My grandmother actually ran a dry cleaner, which inspired this. "A Korean grandmother who has worked in a Brooklyn dry cleaner for thirty years is the only witness who can identify a killer, but she has spent those years pretending not to speak English." Does this work for you? I'd love to hear your opinion.

I keep bees on my roof and have been writing a lullaby for them, which sounds silly out loud. Here's the chorus. Would you mind telling me what you think?
Forty thousand sisters and none of them asks why,
they carry out the winter and they carry in July.
I've been trying to learn how a thing so small
can work like it's the only one and still be one of all.

I've been a landlord for 15 years, and I've seen too many deposit fights. My app idea is Day One. At move-in, tenant and landlord walk through together. The app guides them room by room, with a required photo of each wall, floor and appliance. Each photo is timestamped and cryptographically hashed. At the end, both sign and get the same PDF. Would tenants actually use this? What do you think?

Long-time fantasy reader, first-time writer here. My novel begins: "Tuesday was the day Thornwick hid its children, so the dragon's tax collector found only goats, a very old man, and an unusually loud silence." Would you tell me what you think? Be gentle, I'm a bit anxious about this.

I'm 11 and my idea for an app is called Pet Shift. My family has one dog and four people, and he keeps getting fed twice. You tap "Fed Biscuit" once. If someone else tries to tap it within two hours, the phone says "Dad already fed Biscuit 12 minutes ago." Then it shows a picture of Biscuit looking guilty. What do you think? My mom said to ask someone who knows apps.
Hi, I do freelance branding and I'm sharing a line for an umbrella brand that sells to windy coastal towns: "Built for the wind that ruins other umbrellas." What's your take?

I'm a sonar-tech student, and I tried writing a drama about it. "A submarine sonar operator realizes the whale she has tracked for years is singing her late father's navy radio call sign, and that the pattern has begun to count down." Would you mind giving me your opinion?

Bootcamp student here. I needed to turn nested config into flat keys and ended up with this recursive version. How would you rate it?
```js
const flat = (o, p = '') =>
  Object.entries(o).flatMap(([k, v]) =>
    v && typeof v === 'object' ? flat(v, p + k + '.') : [[p + k, v]]);
Object.fromEntries(flat({ a: { b: 1, c: { d: 2 } } }));
```

I run a small ferry and whale-watching business. Captain Joan retires this weekend, and I'll say: "Joan has crossed this bay nine thousand times and still points at the water like she's never seen it. Tourists come for whales. They stay because she makes them look. Joan, you taught us the sea isn't a show, it's a conversation. Fair winds. Your chair stays at the wheel, facing out." What do you think?

I'm a weekend woodworker selling at a craft fair, and this is my sign copy. "End-grain walnut and maple board, 14 x 10 inches. Knife edges sink between the fibers and the grain closes behind them, so your blades stay sharper and the board shows fewer scars. Finished with mineral oil and beeswax. About six pounds, heavy enough to stay put while you chop." Any thoughts?

units: Thesis paragraph from my philosophy paper: "Nozick assumes we refuse the experience machine because we want contact with reality. That, not the missing real world, is what we'd mourn." Does the argument hold together?

I do funeral photography and I'm starting a dark comedy. Logline: "A professional mourner who attends the funerals of the friendless finds herself at her estranged father's service, where no one else has shown up and her professional standards are on the line." Curious what you think!

What's your opinion?

What do you think about this idea?

I knit and sell sweaters, and I wrote this to work out cast-on counts from my gauge. What's your opinion?
```python
def cast_on(width_cm, stitches_per_10cm, repeat=4, edge=2):
    """Round to the nearest pattern repeat, then add edge stitches."""
    raw = width_cm * stitches_per_10cm / 10
    return round(raw / repeat) * repeat + edge
```

Retired DBA here, tinkering for fun. I wrote an org chart query for our club's volunteer table. Cycle guard included, since people enter data badly:
WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (
  SELECT id, name, manager_id, name::text AS path, 0 AS depth FROM staff WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id, c.path || ' > ' || e.name, c.depth + 1
  FROM staff e JOIN chain c ON e.manager_id = c.id WHERE c.depth < 12)
SELECT * FROM chain ORDER BY path;
What's your opinion?

Every book on this shelf was somebody's Tuesday night,

I just keep the kettle on and the lamp lit low,
and the dead keep writing to whoever's up.

units: Here's one I've been saving for my chess club's newsletter: "My chess rating is like my houseplants: technically alive, and no one is sure why." I'm pretty nervous about sharing it since some of those guys are brutal. How would you rate it?

Hi! I'm sending this to my manager at the coffee shop tomorrow. Here it is:
"Hi Dana, I have organic chemistry finals May 6 and 9, so I can't do my Thursday closes those weeks. Priya and Marcus both said they'd take them if I cover their Sunday opens on the 12th and 19th. I've already put the swaps in the shared sheet. If anything clashes, I'm happy to rework it. Thanks, Leo"
What do you think?
I'm a retired sailor who now makes waxed canvas bags. Slogan for the tag: "Carried through worse weather than this." I'd like to hear what you think.

I wrote this for my little brother, whose dad works nights. "The House Is Wearing Its Quiet." Every afternoon Theo tiptoes through the rooms like they're a sleeping animal: cereal without crunching, cartoons on captions only. At four o'clock Dad's alarm rings, and the whole house exhales and gets loud again. How does it read to you? Be straight with me.

Hi! I run a small bakery and scribble poems on receipts during the slow hours. This is the latest:
At four a.m. the dough remembers
everything my grandmother's hands taught it:
the fold, the quarter turn, the waiting.
I only lend it my arms.
By six, the whole street smells of her.
Honest thoughts welcome!

I own a small dumpling restaurant and I'm writing about my mum for the website. Title: "How to Fold a Dumpling Like My Mother Without Her Hands." First line: "My mother's hands folded eighteen pleats without looking, and after her stroke I had to learn to describe in words what her fingers had never needed to say." I'd be grateful to hear what you think.

Here's my allotment budget, averaged monthly: £42. Plot rent £14, seeds £6, compost and manure £9, netting and slug control £4, tool replacements £5, water butt fund £4. By my tally the veg I'd otherwise buy comes to about £55. Honestly just curious what a fresh set of eyes thinks!

My little cousin stutters, and I wrote this for him. Caleb notices the river stutters too, tripping over every rock ("b-b-bubble, b-b-bubble"), yet it reaches the sea every single time. Nobody in the book ever says "fix." He just sits beside the water and talks back to it. I'm a bit nervous about getting it right. Would you mind giving me honest feedback?

I've been given the lease on a lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Northumberland coast, and I'm turning it into a cafe. The name is "Last Light." We'll close at dusk, so you can watch the lamp come on while you finish your tea. I'm 62 and a bit sentimental about it. What's your reaction to the name?

I'm a retired machinist and now I do science fairs with kids. This year's project: does a pendulum's period change with amplitude as much as the equation says? We'll film a 1 m pendulum at 5°, 15°, 30°, 45°, and 60° with a 240 fps phone camera, extract the period frame by frame, and compare it to the small-angle formula and the elliptic-integral correction. We'd like to know how this comes across.

units: Nervous about sharing this, but here's the thesis for my game design class essay: "Tetris endures not because it is simple but because it is unwinnable: its design turns inevitable failure into a measure of skill, teaching players to take pleasure in managing loss rather than avoiding it." Would love your reaction.

Pastry chef here, testing this for our autumn menu. Pear and rye tart: rye flour pâte sucrée, filled with brown butter frangipane (120g butter, browned and cooled; 120g almond flour; 100g sugar; 2 eggs). Fan thin slices of roasted Bosc pear on top, then glaze with thyme-infused honey and finish with flaky salt. Bake at 175°C for 38 minutes. I'd love an outside opinion before it goes on the menu.

I'm a vet tech and my colleagues keep telling me to write down the stuff I say. This one came up on Tuesday: "Every vet knows the animal is rarely the one who needs sedating." I'd love to hear what someone outside the clinic thinks.

I've been struggling and finally wrote this to my manager. I'm nervous. Can you tell me how it reads?
"Hi Lena, I need to be upfront: I've been running on empty since the audit and my work is slipping. I'd like to take the five leave days I have left next week, then talk about moving the Q3 report to someone else. I'd rather tell you now than miss it."

I'm a mycology student making a logo for our research group. A mushroom is seen from underneath in a single deep brown, with its gills radiating out from the stem. The gills are drawn as fingerprint ridges, so the whole cap looks like a thumbprint. The group name is set in small capitals around the edge in a circle. How does it read to you?

I'm a mechanic, 52, and my daughter says I should show somebody this. So here goes. Tell me what you think.
Under the hood the engine's cooled to a tick,
a metal clock winding down its day.
I wipe my hands on a rag that's been
every color of every car I've loved.

I'm 16 and I'd like to redo Eratosthenes. I teamed up with a student at a school 410 km due north of mine through an online club. On the same day at local solar noon, we each measure a vertical stick's shadow and compute the sun angle, then use the angle difference and the distance to estimate Earth's circumference. I'll also propagate the measurement uncertainty to see whether we can tell our answer apart from 40,075 km. Thoughts?

I'm a hobbyist game designer. Memory-care homes seem to run on bingo, so I made a kit: large tiles with photos of 1950s kitchen objects that residents match and talk about, plus a facilitator card with three open questions. $65 per kit. One activity director tried it, and residents were still chatting after 40 minutes. I'd like to sell it to care homes. What's your take?

I teach piano in a rural village and I'm making a logo for my studio, called Flock Music. Five staff lines roll like green hills. Perched on the lines as notes are little sheep: a round woolly body for the note head and a thin stem upward for the tail. One black sheep is a note in the middle. What do you think of the idea?

I've played jazz piano for thirty years but only recently started writing my own lyrics. Here's a ballad chorus:
The moon is a borrowed coat tonight
Too wide in the shoulders, it still smells of you
I wear it down the avenue
Pretending that it's mine, pretending that it's new
I'd value your impressions.

units: I'm a nursing student and wrote this for my evidence-based practice course. "Among night-shift med-surg nurses, does a protected 20-minute nap at 3 a.m. reduce medication-administration near-misses in the final three hours of the shift, compared with no scheduled break?" Could you give me your honest opinion? I'm a little nervous about it.

Flattening JSON order items in Postgres. Our orders come from three vendors, so the key isn't always present:
SELECT o.id, item->>'sku' AS sku, (item->>'qty')::int AS qty
FROM orders o
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(o.payload->'items') AS item
WHERE o.payload ? 'items';
Backend dev, 2 years of experience. I'd like your thoughts, especially on whether I'm missing something.

I own a little flower shop and wrote this on my lunch break. Showing it to you first, before anyone I know:
I can tell which bouquets will be forgiven
by how the man holds them:
like a question,
or like an alibi.
How does it read to you?

Hey, this is from my intro DB class project (a book review site). I wanted the top 3 rated books in each category:
SELECT c.name AS category, t.title, t.rating
FROM categories c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT b.title, b.rating FROM books b
  WHERE b.category_id = c.id
  ORDER BY b.rating DESC, b.title
  LIMIT 3) t
ORDER BY c.name, t.rating DESC;
Would love to hear what you think!

Here's a Threads post I wrote about a film I love, would love your take: "Spirited Away is the only movie I know where the scariest scene is a man being kind to you. No-Face's loneliness works because nobody in the bathhouse ever asks what he actually wants."

I'm a night-shift nurse and cook when I'm exhausted, so this is a one-pot dinner. Toast 2 tsp cumin seeds in olive oil, add onion, garlic, then 1½ cups red lentils and 6 cups water. Simmer 20 minutes. Stir in the chopped rind of half a preserved lemon, finish with lots of black pepper and a spoon of yogurt. Chili butter on top. Does this sound like something worth making again?

I'm a plumber and I came up with this for the side of my van: "Every house has one pipe that's been quietly holding a grudge since 1974." My wife says it's too long for a van. Be straight with me: would you read it, and would you call me?

Pareto analysis for our catalogue: what share of revenue the top products make. I added the tie-breaker and ROWS frame deliberately.
WITH r AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(revenue) AS rev FROM sales GROUP BY product_id)
SELECT product_id, rev,
  SUM(rev) OVER (ORDER BY rev DESC, product_id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) / SUM(rev) OVER () AS cum_share
FROM r ORDER BY rev DESC, product_id;
I'm a finance manager, not a developer. Does this look right to you?

I'm 16, a goalkeeper, and season starts in six weeks. Mon: box jumps 4x4, band-resisted lateral shuffles. Tue: team practice. Wed: pull-ups 4x6, Nordic curls 3x5, Copenhagen planks. Thu: practice, then 10 minutes of tennis-ball reaction catches off a wall. Fri: mobility only. Sat: match. Sun: easy swim, shoulder prehab. Nothing heavy within 48 hours of a match, so I planned around that. Any thoughts? Be straight with me.

I'm a vet, and I want to start a dental plan for pets. $19 a month covers a yearly scaling under anesthesia, a home-brushing kit, and a video call with a tech every quarter to check your technique. I've seen too many dogs lose teeth at eight because the cleaning cost $600 at once. My plan makes that cost small and regular. Be honest, would you sign up your own dog?

units: Just graduated and applying for backend jobs. This is the first bullet under my internship: "Reduced p95 checkout API latency from 1.8s to 310ms by replacing N+1 Postgres queries with batched lookups and adding a read-through Redis cache, saving an estimated $42K/yr in compute." What do you think? Anything you'd change?

I'm the groom's boss, and I was asked to speak, which I assume means they ran out of friends. My line: "In six years Hugo has never missed a deadline except one: the Friday he left early to propose. I've never been so glad to be let down. Tess, we got a great employee. You got the rest of him, and I'm told that's the better deal." Thoughts?

I run a bike repair shop and I'm finally writing for our website. Title: "Your Bike Isn't Making That Noise to Annoy You." Opening: "Every click, tick, and groan from a bicycle is a tiny confession, and after eleven years of fixing them above a laundromat, I can usually tell you what yours did last weekend before you finish describing the sound." Feedback welcome!

I'm a chef, and I wrote my best friend's wedding toast as a recipe. Ending: "Method: take two people who argue about salt. Add twelve years, one kitchen fire, and a very patient dog. Do not rush. Season with forgiveness, daily, to taste. Serves everyone at this table, who will leave fuller than they came. Tom, Maria: may you never run out." Honest thoughts?

I'm a retired ferry captain turning a moored barge into a floating cafe. I'm naming it "Dead Reckoning," the old way of finding your position without landmarks, and now it's how I find my way into retirement. How does it strike you?

I'm a physics PhD student and this is my first conference talk, so I'm nervous. I'm opening with: "If the sun were a grapefruit on this lectern, the nearest other grapefruit would be about 2,900 kilometres away, and the space between would hold, on average, nothing." What's your reaction?

I'm a farmer, and I set aside 1 acre on the edge of my property for a wildlife pond and meadow. A 20m x 10m pond with a shallow shelf on the south side, and a deep area of 2.5m on the north. A wildflower meadow, mown only in September, surrounds it, with a hedgerow of hawthorn, blackthorn, and dog rose on the windward side. A log pile and a stone hibernaculum for amphibians sits at the east end. Do you have any feedback?

My used bookshop is called The Dog-Eared Page. For the logo, I imagined a simple page in cream, with its top corner folded down. The fold is shaped as a floppy dog ear, with one small ink dot for an eye on the folded part. Everything else is blank paper. Thoughts? Be as blunt as you like.

Tonight I'm opening our astronomy club's star party. Here's the speech: "The light you'll see in Andromeda left 2.5 million years ago, before anything we'd call human. It has been traveling toward this field, this telescope, this paper cup of cocoa in your hand. Please don't rush. It's waited a long time for you. Red flashlights only, and be kind to the dark." What do you reckon?

units: This is the new homepage copy for my plumbing company: "A $20 valve inspection is boring. A flooded kitchen at 2 a.m. is not. Most of our emergency calls started as a drip someone meant to look at. Book a yearly check, and the only exciting thing in your house will be dinner." Does it sound like a real person wrote it?

Flight instructor here, applying to a regional airline. This is the bullet I lead with: "Instructed 47 students to private pilot certificates with a 94% first-attempt checkride pass rate, versus a 71% national average." Curious how it reads to someone outside aviation. Thoughts?

I'm a 29-year-old climber working toward my first 8a. Mon: 4 max hangs on a 20mm edge (10 s, +5 kg), then limit bouldering. Tue: 40-minute zone-2 bike, core. Wed: rest. Thu: 4x4s on routes two grades below my limit. Fri: push-ups, reverse wrist curls, shoulder external rotation. Sat: project attempts while fresh. Sun: rest. Every fourth week I halve the volume. How does it look to you?

I'm a night-shift nurse and cook when I'm exhausted, so this is a one-pot dinner. Toast 2 tsp cumin seeds in olive oil, add onion, garlic, then 1½ cups red lentils and 6 cups water. Simmer 20 minutes. Stir in the chopped rind of half a preserved lemon, finish with lots of black pepper and a spoon of yogurt. Chili butter on top. Does this sound like something worth making again?

I'm a 911 dispatcher, 48. Here's what I said at Carla's last-shift party: 'Carla has been the first voice on the worst day of ten thousand lives. She never got to see how any of them ended. She just said, "Stay on the line with me," and they did. Tonight, Carla, we're the ones saying it. Stay on the line. Visit. Bring the good cookies.' Nervous to share. Thoughts?

Hey, I run a taco truck. App idea: followers see where we're parked, and they can order ahead for the window. Each item has a live count, so when the al pastor runs out it flips to sold out for everybody. The pickup time comes from the actual number of tickets on the grill. Does that make sense? Curious about your take.

I'm 16 and writing to fund our youth orchestra's trip to Vienna. Here's my opening, and I'm kind of nervous about sending it: "Our second violins have never played anywhere with an echo. This June, we'd like to change that. Thirty-one of us, one cellist who's afraid of planes, and a conductor who has promised not to cry." Does it work as an opening?

I've been home with my kids for 8 years and I'm applying for a project coordinator job. Nervous! Paragraph: "For eight years I've managed a team of three with unpredictable deadlines, no budget, and a 6 a.m. launch every day. I also ran the school auction, which raised $41,000 using one spreadsheet and fifty unreliable volunteers. People call that a transferable skill. I'd like to prove it on yours." Honest reaction, please?

I'm 22, bilingual, and I wrote this chorus about my mom making tortillas before work:
Mi mamá cuenta el mundo en tortillas
One for the rent, one for the rain
Dos para mí, y una para la esperanza
Flip it quick before it burns again
I'd really like to know what you think, especially about mixing the languages.

Posted this on my Instagram story during finals and a few friends replied, but I want a stranger's view: "Finals tip from someone who cried in the library stacks yesterday: you're not behind, you're in the middle. The middle always feels like failure because you can't see either shore. Drink water. Text a friend. Write only the next paragraph."

units: My grandmother takes seven pills a day and gets confused about which she's had. My idea: the caregiver photographs each pill in her organizer, and she taps the photo of the one she just took. No reading required. The family gets one quiet summary each evening, not constant alerts. I'd like to know what you think before I show it to my aunts.

Weekend baker here. My loaf: 500g bread flour, 100g whole wheat, 20g toasted barley flour, with cold roasted barley tea replacing the water (80% hydration). 20% levain, four stretch-and-folds, overnight cold proof, baked covered at 245°C for 20 minutes, then uncovered for 22. Does the formula make sense to you? Any tweaks you'd suggest?
I teach yoga in a small studio above a pharmacy. Here's the slogan I wrote for the door: "Come as you are. Leave a little taller." Could you tell me what you think of it?

I'm a financial adviser and I'm speaking to a room of twenty-somethings. I begin: "Imagine a stranger who will inherit everything you earn this year, and who currently receives none of it. He's you, at sixty-seven." How would you react to that if you were sitting in the audience?

Software engineer by day, haiku hobbyist by night. This one came from a late release:
Deploy at midnight—
rain on the office window
writes its own log lines
Curious how it reads to a non-programmer. Thoughts?

I'm a second-year econ PhD student trying to write for a general audience. Title: "The Bus Fare Is a Lie We Agreed On." Opening: "Every city bus fare is a price set not by what a ride costs but by what a mayor can survive charging, which makes the fare box less a cash register than a weekly opinion poll." Does it work for you?

I'm a barista and I write haiku on receipt paper during slow shifts, lol. Here's one from today:
Rush over. The foam
heart I made begins to blur
toward the cup's edge
what do u think?

I'm a school librarian and an immigrant, and I wrote this one for me too. Linh collects the wrong ways people say her name in jars: Lin, Lynn, Lean. Her grandmother says each jar is a small gift from someone who tried. On the last page, a new teacher asks Linh to say it first. I'd love your thoughts, truly.

I run a food truck (Korean-Mexican, mostly kimchi quesadillas) and wrote my profile in the same spirit. How's it land?
"I feed strangers from a window for twelve hours a day, so I'm excellent at small talk and terrible at days off. Looking for someone to sit on my truck's tailgate at midnight and tell me what I should put on the specials board. I'll pay in quesadillas. Vegetarian options available. I'm not heartless."

I'm 55 and started saving late, so I'm catching up. Take-home $5,400: mortgage 1,450; groceries 500; utilities 280; car 350; health insurance 400; 401k catch-up 1,000; HSA 300; help with my son's college 500; fun 200; misc 420. Feeling a bit anxious about it. How does this look to you?

units:
I drive long-haul and write these at truck stops. This one's from a night in Wyoming:
Wyoming, midnight—
my headlights find one fence post,
then lose it again
Curious what you think of it, especially the ending.

I'm in 6th grade and I'm testing paper airplane winglets. I made a launcher from a ruler and a rubber band pulled back to exactly 10 cm so every launch has the same speed. I'll fold 5 identical planes for each wing design (none, up, down, and split tips), throw each one 10 times, and record the glide distance from a fixed height. Then I'll calculate the glide ratio for each. Does this sound good to you?

I have ADHD and get bored by week two, so my plan has fixed anchors and random variety. Mon legs, Tue push, Thu pull, Sat carries and run. Each day's main lift never changes (squat, press, row, farmer carry). Accessories come from rolling a die against a list of six per day. Wed/Fri: 20-minute walk with podcasts. Sun: off. Tracking is one tick on the fridge. Do you think it holds together?

I taught fourth grade for 34 years and I'm applying to be a docent at the natural history museum. This is my paragraph: "Every September I handed my students a whale vertebra I'd bought at a yard sale and said nothing for a full minute. The questions they asked in that silence taught me more about teaching than any training did. I'd like to bring that minute of silence to your visitors." Could you tell me what you make of it?

I'm a bassist who's been touring for ten years and this has happened to me twice. "When a band's player gets sick the night before a gig, we get a vetted session musician who has already studied their charts and setlist into the van within twelve hours." What do you think?

i'm 22, barista, write poems on receipts. my bio: "I'll remember your order by the third visit and your name by the fifth. Hoping to be remembered back. Currently reading three books, finishing none. Fluent in sarcasm, conversational in Portuguese. If you like rainy bus rides and arguing about whether cereal is soup, hi." thoughts?

I own a small bakery and I'm writing a post to explain our prices. Title: "Why Our Croissants Cost $4.50." First sentence: "A croissant is three days of waiting disguised as breakfast: one day for the dough, one for the butter to settle into it, and one for me to stop touching it." Could you tell me your impressions?

I run a bike repair shop and I'm finally writing for our website. Title: "Your Bike Isn't Making That Noise to Annoy You." Opening: "Every click, tick, and groan from a bicycle is a tiny confession, and after eleven years of fixing them above a laundromat, I can usually tell you what yours did last weekend before you finish describing the sound." Feedback welcome!

Hi! I'm a line cook, six years in, applying for a sous chef job. Here's the middle paragraph of my letter: "At Marlow's I cut our walk-in waste from 14% to 5% by turning trim into the staff meal, then the staff meal into a Thursday special that outsold the ribeye. I'm not interested in cooking expensive food. I'm interested in making sure nothing that enters your kitchen dies in the bin." Honest thoughts?

I work as a wildlife biologist and carry a little notebook on surveys. This is from an elk count in October:
Dawn on the ridge trail—
my breath and the elk's breath hang
in the same cold air
What's your opinion of it?

units:
Latest reading per sensor, for a dashboard that refreshes every few seconds. I'm an IoT hobbyist with a Raspberry Pi and a lot of sensors:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (sensor_id) sensor_id, recorded_at, temp_c
FROM readings
WHERE recorded_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
ORDER BY sensor_id, recorded_at DESC;
I also have an index on (sensor_id, recorded_at DESC). Any feedback would be great!

I run a little toy shop and wrote a fable for the kids who come in on Saturdays. Here's how it begins. Would you tell me what you think? "Once there was a clock that was always seven minutes slow, and the town loved it for exactly that reason. Late for church? Blame the clock. Late for love? The clock. It carried the town's small sins like a mule, until the day a clockmaker arrived, tool bag in hand, offering to help."

I'm 14 and I like music, so I'm doing Chladni plates. I'm bolting a 20 cm square aluminum plate to a speaker driver, sprinkling salt on it, and sweeping frequencies from 100 to 3000 Hz. I'll photograph each pattern at resonance, then compare the frequencies to the theoretical plate-mode formula to find which ones match. I'll also test how the patterns change when I clamp the plate at its center vs. its edge. What do you think?
so my brother and I started a small tea company in our garage and this is the slogan I drafted lol: "Sit down. It's steeping." Be honest, what do you think?

I run a true-crime podcast as a hobby and wrote an essay about the genre. Thesis: "True-crime podcasts promise justice but deliver intimacy: the genre's appeal lies less in solving cases than in the feeling of being trusted with a stranger's worst day, one episode at a time." What do you think?

I design board games as a hobby and I'm giving a talk at a small convention. I'm opening with: "The most important rule in my game is on the back of the box, in small type: 'The player who is winning may not know it.'" What's your opinion?

I'm 55 and started saving late, so I'm catching up. Take-home $5,400: mortgage 1,450; groceries 500; utilities 280; car 350; health insurance 400; 401k catch-up 1,000; HSA 300; help with my son's college 500; fun 200; misc 420. Feeling a bit anxious about it. How does this look to you?

I run a pottery studio and I'm starting a scholarship fund for teens. The letter opens: "Clay doesn't care about your grades. It doesn't care who your parents are, or whether you've eaten today. It only cares whether you're paying attention. We'd like to offer fifteen teenagers a seat at the wheel, free, for a year." How does it read to you?

Hi! I'm 16 and I made these for my family's New Year dinner and I'm kind of nervous about sharing. Black sesame shortbread: 200g butter, 90g powdered sugar, 250g flour, 40g toasted ground black sesame, 1 tbsp orange zest, ½ tsp salt. Chill the dough 1 hour, slice, then roll the edges in raw sesame seeds. Bake at 160°C for 22 minutes. Could you tell me what you think?

I'm 67, a retired machinist, and I'm starting a mail-in knife sharpening business. My pitch card says: "Send us your dull knife. We'll send you a sharp loaner the same day, so dinner never waits. Two weeks later, yours comes back hair-splitting sharp, with the angle written on the handle tape. $12 a knife. Return shipping is on us." Be straight with me, what do you make of it?
