units:
I'm a hobbyist drone photographer and want to pitch a hotel manager. Here's the email:
"Dear Ms. Aoki, I'm a local photographer, and last week at golden hour I shot your hotel's rooftop terrace from above, attached. The frame shows the pool, the hills behind, and the sunset hitting the cabanas. I'd be glad to shoot a full set of ten images for your website for $250. I'm licensed to fly in this area. May I send a quote? Regards, Daniel"
What do you think?

I translate Korean webtoons as a fan hobby, and I'm applying for a junior localization job. This is my cover letter paragraph on translation philosophy. What do you make of it?
"In one series, a character says '밥 먹었어?' to mean 'I love you.' A literal translation says 'Did you eat?' A faithful one says something else entirely. I've learned to keep the question and add the worry around it: 'Have you eaten yet? You look tired.'"

Because I forget things, my budget is automated on payday (TA income $1,700). Rent $720 and utilities $55 autopay; $200 auto-savings; $60 'forgetful tax' fund for late fees and lost stuff; groceries $250; phone $35; transit $70; books $60; $200 weekly cash envelopes ($50 × 4) for fun; $50 buffer. What do you think of the system?

Preserved lemon and olive chicken. Marinate thighs overnight in ras el hanout, grated onion, ginger and saffron steeped in warm water. Brown, then braise over low heat on a bed of onions with no added water for 45 minutes. Add the rind of one preserved lemon (pith removed) and green olives for the last 15 minutes. Finish with cilantro. Would you adjust anything?

I'm opening a chess café named En Passant. The logo is a pawn in solid black, front-on. But its round head is a coffee cup seen from above: a ring, dark liquid inside, and a small handle at the right side where a pawn would have nothing. Everything else is perfectly standard. I'd like your opinion, please.

Stand-up comic, 26, and I finally wrote a bio I'm ready to post. "I'm funnier in person, which is the worst thing a comedian can put on a dating app. Five-six, or six if the shoes are loud. I will make a joke about our first fight during our first fight. Looking for someone who can take a punchline and deliver a better one." Be honest!

Hi! I'm 16 and this is the first logline I've written for a film project in my media class: "When her father, a small-town marching band director, slowly loses his hearing, a teenage drum major secretly conducts the band from the field while he believes he's still leading it." Could you tell me what you think?

I run a pet-sitting business and I'm emailing the manager of the kennel I partner with. Here goes:
"Hi Greta, over July 4th weekend, I'd like to reserve five overflow kennels for my regular clients. All five dogs are vaccinated, and I'll send their records by Friday. I'll drop off, feed, and walk them myself, so there's no extra work for your staff. I can pay $200 up front. Could you confirm by the 20th? Thanks, Marcus"
What do you think?

I'm the mayor of a town of 6,000 and I'm campaigning for the library levy. Here's a section of my speech: "A library is the last place in town where you can walk in with no money and nobody asks why you're there. It costs the average household $41 a year. Ask yourself what else you can buy that's open to everyone, including the person you'd never think of." How does that sit with you?

I'm 40 and have never lifted before, so I kept it simple. Mon/Wed/Fri: goblet squat, dumbbell bench, one-arm row, Romanian deadlift, plank, always in that order. Start at 3x8, add one rep per week until 3x12, then add weight. Tue/Thu: 20-minute walk. Sat: something fun. Sun: rest. I write down how I felt after each session. I'm a bit nervous about sharing it. What do you think?

units: I'm a first-generation college student writing a novel inspired by my family. Here's the opening line: "My mother carried two suitcases across the border: one for what we owned, and one, empty, for what we would be given." I'd be grateful to hear what you think of it.

I'm a beekeeper with six hives, and I planned a 10m x 10m forage garden to support them from March to October. Early: crocus, willow, and hellebores. Spring: lungwort, borage, and fruit blossoms. Summer: lime tree, phacelia, and marjoram. Autumn: ivy, Sedum, and asters. Hives are in the southeast corner, facing away from the path, with a 2m hedge forcing bees to fly up. What do you think of it?

Hello! This is my winter-interest border for Minnesota, 10x30 ft along the garage. Red twig dogwood at the back for stem colour against the snow. Mid layer: switchgrass 'Northwind' and sedum 'Matrona', both left standing. A paper birch cluster at the east end with white bark glowing at sunrise. Hellebores are tucked in near the door, so there's something to see on the shortest days. I'd like to know what you think!

First-gen student here. I wrote this hook after an internship interview and I'm kind of nervous to show anyone. What's your honest take?
Mama dusted the boardroom where I'm interviewing now,
she knew the table's every scar and never knew how
to ask for a seat there. So I'll sit, and I'll stay,
with her name in my mouth like the first thing I say.

I'm a tailor with a 12-year-old shop. New service: 'Bought It, Fit It.' People order clothes online and ship them straight to me. After one measurement video call, I alter and send them on for a flat $35. My notes stay on file, so future orders get fixed before they even arrive. I think it turns returns into repeat customers. What do you think?

I'm a line cook who got curious about browning. I'll caramelize identical onion slices in solutions of baking soda at five different pH levels, then photograph each batch every 5 minutes next to a gray card and convert the pixels to L*a*b* color values. Then I'll plot how fast browning happens against pH. I'm a little nervous presenting at a science fair as a non-scientist. What do you think of it?

I've been a carpenter for forty years and this is my first story. The narrator is a house. "The Pattersons took the couch, the lamps, and the cat. They left me the height marks on the kitchen doorframe, which I thought was kind." Then it waits for the next family. What's your take on it?

I'm into amateur radio, and this is my idea. Two ESP32 LoRa boards log signal strength (RSSI) at 25 m intervals through dense forest and across an open field of the same length. I'll fit a path-loss model to both and compare the exponents. I'll repeat in summer and after leaf drop. I'm kind of proud of this one. What's your take?

I've been given the lease on a lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Northumberland coast, and I'm turning it into a cafe. The name is "Last Light." We'll close at dusk, so you can watch the lamp come on while you finish your tea. I'm 62 and a bit sentimental about it. What's your reaction to the name?

Hobby beekeeper here, and I'm a little proud of this one. I'd lease rooftop hives to restaurants for $85 a month. I handle all inspections, and they get 20 jars a year labelled with their street name, plus a QR code to a short video of 'their' bees. Chefs get a menu story, and I fund my other 12 hives. Three owners have said they're interested. Does it seem worth pursuing?

units:
I'm a ham radio hobbyist applying to be a 911 dispatcher. Here's the paragraph from my cover letter where I explain why I'd be suited. What's your opinion?
"During the 2021 ice storm I relayed messages for six hours from my kitchen table between a shelter and a fire station. What I remember is how quiet I got. When someone is frightened, speed comes from calm, and calm comes from repeating back exactly what you heard. I'd bring that habit to your center."

Hello, I'm a brewer starting Low Tide Brewing. The logo is a pint glass in outline. The foam line at the top is a flat horizon, and below it, the beer is filled with faint sand ripples, the pattern left on a beach when the water goes out. One line weight throughout, cream on navy. I'd really like your take on it.

I run a one-item dumpling food truck and I'm pitching to a festival committee next week. Here's how I'm starting: "My truck sells exactly one thing, a dumpling, and in the next ten minutes I'm going to convince you that's a strategy and not a limitation." Can you tell me your opinion?

Student cooking for my flatmates. My cacio e pepe variation: toast black pepper and 1 tsp red Sichuan peppercorns, crush coarsely. Cook 100g tonnarelli in very little water so the starch stays high, and pull it 2 minutes early. Off the heat, mix Pecorino with pasta water into a paste first, then toss everything together with the pepper. Can you give me feedback on the technique?

We're farmers and just started jarring pickles. My wife says I should ask strangers what they think. Here's the label text:
"Dill spears from our back field, picked at breakfast, jarred by lunch. Garlic, dill heads, sea salt, and a grape leaf to keep them crunchy. No sugar, no vinegar, just a warm week on the counter. Open one on a hot day. Once opened, they keep two months in the fridge, though they rarely last a week."

Monthly cohort retention for our subscription app. I'm a data scientist and wrote it in one sitting, so tell me if I've missed something.
WITH f AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(date_trunc('month', ordered_at)) AS cohort
  FROM orders GROUP BY 1)
SELECT f.cohort,
  DATEDIFF('month', f.cohort, date_trunc('month', o.ordered_at)) AS months_since,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS active
FROM f JOIN orders o USING (customer_id)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2;

I run a little hardware store and wrote a rhyming book. Here's how it opens:
"When the owner turns the sign and the keys click twice,
the hammers call to order and the washers roll dice;
the tape measures argue about who's most long,
and the level says, 'Friends, you are all slightly wrong.'"
What do you think? I'm curious whether the rhythm holds up when read aloud.

ok so my mate dared me to write something funny. Opening of my story:
"Gary Pemberton-Voss had been a respectable supervillain for eleven years when his henchmen unionised. By Thursday the volcano lair had a grievance procedure, mandatory tea breaks, and a laminated sign: PLEASE DO NOT ADDRESS THE SHARKS DURING LUNCH. Gary, who had once held a city to ransom, found he could not win an argument about dental."
Does it land?

Weekend gardener here, and my zucchini has gotten completely out of hand. I turned it into a country chorus. Be straight with me, what's your take?
Zucchini in July, please, I'm begging you stop,
I've left bags on porches, I've filled the church shop.
The neighbors all wave with a too-careful smile.
They've seen me coming up the drive for a mile.

WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, login_at::date AS d FROM logins),
g AS (SELECT user_id, d, d - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY d))::int AS grp FROM d)

g AS (SELECT user_id, d, d - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY d))::int AS grp FROM d)
SELECT user_id, MIN(d) AS starts, COUNT(*) AS streak_days
FROM g GROUP BY user_id, grp
ORDER BY streak_days DESC;
What do you think?
</message>

I make a small podcast about local history from my closet, and I'm applying for a radio producer job. Here's the paragraph on my work. Can you tell me what you think?
"Episode 14 is eleven minutes about the 1952 flood, and nine of them are one woman, Dolores, describing the sound of the river at night. I cut my own questions to almost nothing. A producer's job, I've learned, is to build a quiet room and then leave it."

History major here, posted this thread opener and I'm hoping for honest feedback: "The Library of Alexandria didn't burn in one dramatic night. It faded the way libraries do: budgets cut, scholars leaving, scrolls not recopied. Knowledge is lost less like a bonfire and more like a slow leak. Worth remembering when we trim library hours."

Hey, I coach distance runners and write a small newsletter. Next post is titled "Mile 20 Is a Negotiation." I open with: "Nobody warns you that at mile twenty your body will open with a lowball offer, and the whole skill of the sport is knowing it's only the first one." Could you tell me how this reads to you?

I coach a running club and I'm writing my first screenplay. Logline: "A blind marathoner's guide runner begins to lose his own sight, and neither man tells the other." I'm a bit nervous putting it out there. What's your take?

Here's my bio for a climbing-gym meetup app. I'm a hobbyist climber, nothing fancy. Does it work?
"I'm a 5.10 climber with a 5.13 vocabulary for complaining about it. Strong opinions: chalk bags should be washed, belay attention should be absolute, and the best part of any route is the sitting-down afterward. Looking for a partner who'll catch my falls and my terrible puns, in that order."

I run a little pottery studio and want to stop guessing about cracking. Here's what I wrote in my notebook: "Does adding 5% grog by weight to our stoneware body reduce cracking in pieces thicker than 2 cm during bisque firing at a ramp of 100°C per hour?" I'd fire matched test tiles. Does this seem like a good question to you?

I keep aquariums, and I'm trying duckweed as a nitrate sensor. I'll grow 10 fronds per jar in 0, 5, 20, and 50 ppm nitrate, then photograph from above every day for 12 days. ImageJ gives me the green area, which I'll use to calculate the growth rate. Three replicates, same light and temperature. Could I get your opinion on it?

Here's a Threads post I wrote about a film I love, would love your take: "Spirited Away is the only movie I know where the scariest scene is a man being kind to you. No-Face's loneliness works because nobody in the bathhouse ever asks what he actually wants."

I've been running tabletop RPG campaigns for friends for years and I'm trying to break into game design. Here's my resume bullet: "Designed and ran a 3-year campaign for 7 players; rewrote the combat system after playtests showed fights averaging 94 minutes, cutting them to 35 while preserving player choice." Any feedback?

I run a small bakery and wrote this haiku during a 4 a.m. shift:
Flour dusts my wrists—
the oven ticks, half awake,
before the first bird.
Could you tell me what you think of it?

I'm a hobbyist stargazer and I wrote this for my granddaughter. "Marguerite Counts Satellites." Every clear night she and her grandpa lie on their shop roof counting the moving stars. She's told to wish on the first one, but she names them instead. When one burns up and vanishes, she writes it a goodbye. I'm wondering how a six-year-old would take it. What's your reaction?

I sell empanadas from a food truck and I'm writing the market manager. I'm excited but a bit nervous:
"Hi Ms. Lindqvist, I've been at the Saturday market for 14 weeks and sold out by 1 p.m. every time. Could I move from the back lot to the corner near the fountain? The line currently blocks no one, but at the corner I could double the queue space. I'd also add a compostable-packaging pledge. Happy to chat. Warmly, Valentina"

Self-employed plumber, three kids. I pay myself $6,000 a month from the business. Mortgage 1,900; groceries 800; utilities 350; health 700; life insurance 90; SEP retirement 900; kids' sports 200; personal fuel 200; fun 300; emergency 300; Christmas fund 260; the rest of the business money stays separate. Be straight with me. What do you reckon?

the gulls and I agree on
what is worth keeping
Honest thoughts welcome, I can take it.

Nursing student here, about to put this on my profile. Can you tell me what you think?
Good at: finding a vein first try, parallel parking, remembering your dog's name.
Working on: sourdough, leaving the group chat on read, believing me when I say "I'm fine."
Night rotations mean my weekends are Tuesdays. If you can be cheerful about dinner at 8 a.m., we'll get along.

I run a little hardware store and wrote a rhyming book. Here's how it opens:
"When the owner turns the sign and the keys click twice,
the hammers call to order and the washers roll dice;
the tape measures argue about who's most long,
and the level says, 'Friends, you are all slightly wrong.'"
What do you think? I'm curious whether the rhythm holds up when read aloud.

I'm 15 and I'm entering a science fair with a bioplastic I made. My intro is: "This is a bag made from last Sunday's potato peels. In six weeks it will be soil, which is more than the bag it replaces can promise in six hundred years." What do you think?

Music theory student here, and I'm opening my class presentation at the piano: "Play any two notes a half-step apart and you'll feel uneasy. That unease is why the shark in Jaws works, and I'm going to show you how to make it with two fingers." Would love to hear what you think.

I'm a student and wrote a short poem for my Instagram, kind of nervous to ask but what do you think? "My grandmother counts in two languages: / Polish for coins and stairs, / English for the days since Dziadek, / and for the rosary, no language, / only the click of the next bead."

units: I'm a line cook who got curious about browning. I'll caramelize identical onion slices in solutions of baking soda at five different pH levels, then photograph each batch every 5 minutes next to a gray card and convert the pixels to L*a*b* color values. Then I'll plot how fast browning happens against pH. I'm a little nervous presenting at a science fair as a non-scientist. What do you think of it?

I'm a locksmith with a small business, and my daughter talked me into blogging. Title: "Locked Out at 2 a.m.: A Locksmith's Field Guide to Humility." First sentence: "Nobody calls me because they're having a good night, so the first thing I do on every job is say something small and kind, because the door is the easy part." What do you make of it?

Stand-up comic, 26, and I finally wrote a bio I'm ready to post. "I'm funnier in person, which is the worst thing a comedian can put on a dating app. Five-six, or six if the shoes are loud. I will make a joke about our first fight during our first fight. Looking for someone who can take a punchline and deliver a better one." Be honest!

My small city yard is 15x30 ft, so I made a four-bed rotation plan: Bed A brassicas, Bed B legumes and peas, Bed C tomatoes, peppers and basil, Bed D roots and alliums. Each moves one bed clockwise every year, and compost goes on whichever bed is next to host the tomatoes. Cover crop of crimson clover fills any gap in winter. A 2 ft path loop keeps everything within arm's reach. Opinions?

I'm 68 and retired, and I'm sick of mosquito-repelling phone apps. For my grandson's fair, we'll build a two-chamber choice box with a screen divider, put in 20 fruit flies, and then play the app's tone on only one side. A blinded helper chooses the side with a coin flip. After 10 minutes we count the flies per side. Then we'll repeat it 30 times and run a binomial test. What's your opinion?

I'm 71 and I sell jam at farmers' markets under my family name, Marlow's. For the logo I scanned the M from my late mother's recipe card, her actual handwriting, and traced it cleanly. Where the dot of ink had pooled at the end of the last stroke, I replaced it with a small thumbprint in jam red. Everything else is plain. I'd welcome your opinion.

I make kombucha to sell at the farmers' market, and I'm designing a project about its pH during fermentation. I'll brew five identical 1 L jars, and test pH with a calibrated meter every 12 hours for 14 days. I'll also record the temperature, and taste-test safely only after day 7. The graph should show when it crosses pH 3.5. What would you say about the design?

I'm a 1600-rated club chess player writing up a project for fun. My question: "For players rated 1400 to 1800 in 15+10 online games, do time-trouble blunders cost more rating points than opening errors, and does that balance shift after a player's first thirty games?" I'd use Lichess data. Would love any opinion you have!

I farm soybeans in Iowa and I wrote a novel over a few winters. First line: "Every spring my father buried something in the north field, and every autumn he pretended not to know where." Not sure who to ask out here, so I'm asking you. What do you think?

Preserved lemon and olive chicken. Marinate thighs overnight in ras el hanout, grated onion, ginger and saffron steeped in warm water. Brown, then braise over low heat on a bed of onions with no added water for 45 minutes. Add the rind of one preserved lemon (pith removed) and green olives for the last 15 minutes. Finish with cilantro. Would you adjust anything?

```python
def atomic_write(path, data):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=d)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
            f.write(data)
            f.flush()
            os.fsync(f.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except BaseException:
        os.unlink(tmp)
        raise
```

units: I'm 16 and I made a plan for our tiny 1.5m x 3m balcony to help pollinators. West-facing, so hot. Back rail: lavender in long troughs. Hanging baskets along the front with nasturtiums, trailing down so there's something flowering from April to October. Do you have any thoughts?

I own three laundromats in Cleveland and I'm nervous about sharing this. My pitch: "I'll license the software I wrote that lets customers reserve a specific machine and get a text when their cycle ends, at $40 per location monthly, because it cut my idle machine time by 22%." Honest thoughts?

I sing alto in our community choir and I'm making the fundraising appeal at the spring concert. "We've never been a loud choir. You fall asleep mid-sentence, mid-sock, mid-spoon,
a small sun going down in stages.
I carry you the way you'd carry soup,
all of me arranged around not spilling.

units: I own a tiny bookshop and I'm launching 'Flights.' For $12 you fill in a short taste form (it includes 'a book you gave up on, and why'), and I choose three books for you. Keep one, return two unmarked within 14 days, and your $12 comes back as store credit. Returned books go on a 'flown once' shelf at 40% off. Opinions welcome!

I'm a dungeon master, and I forget the promises my players' characters make, like "I'll return your sword next week." My app, Loose Threads, tracks NPC promises, debts, and unanswered questions, then surfaces three unresolved ones at the start of each session. You can tie each thread to a character. Thoughts? I'd like to know if other DMs would find it useful.

I'm 16, a goalkeeper, and season starts in six weeks. Mon: box jumps 4x4, band-resisted lateral shuffles. Tue: team practice. Wed: pull-ups 4x6, Nordic curls 3x5, Copenhagen planks. Thu: practice, then 10 minutes of tennis-ball reaction catches off a wall. Fri: mobility only. Sat: match. Sun: easy swim, shoulder prehab. Nothing heavy within 48 hours of a match, so I planned around that. Any thoughts? Be straight with me.

Retired DBA here, tinkering for fun. I wrote an org chart query for our club's volunteer table. Cycle guard included, since people enter data badly:
WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (
  SELECT id, name, manager_id, name::text AS path, 0 AS depth FROM staff WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id, c.path || ' > ' || e.name, c.depth + 1
  FROM staff e JOIN chain c ON e.manager_id = c.id WHERE c.depth < 12)
SELECT * FROM chain ORDER BY path;
What's your opinion?

I'm a marine engineer starting a sailboat rigging business, Bowline Marine. The mark is a rope tied in a bowline, drawn as one thick line in navy. The loop of the knot forms the bowl of a capital B, and the standing part runs down as its stem. The working end of the rope tucks behind, and you can follow the knot correctly. Does it hold up, in your view?

Hobby beekeeper here, and I'm a little proud of this one. I'd lease rooftop hives to restaurants for $85 a month. I handle all inspections, and they get 20 jars a year labelled with their street name, plus a QR code to a short video of 'their' bees. Chefs get a menu story, and I fund my other 12 hives. Three owners have said they're interested. Does it seem worth pursuing?

Hey, this is from my intro DB class project (a book review site). I wanted the top 3 rated books in each category:
SELECT c.name AS category, t.title, t.rating
FROM categories c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT b.title, b.rating FROM books b
  WHERE b.category_id = c.id
  ORDER BY b.rating DESC, b.title
  LIMIT 3) t
ORDER BY c.name, t.rating DESC;
Would love to hear what you think!

Proud to finally share this. I'm a Mumbai-based sound editor, 52, and it's the first story I've written myself: "In 1950s Bombay, the unseen playback singer behind a film star's voice must decide whether to expose her when the star's husband falls in love with the voice and not the woman." How does it strike you?

Language-learning student here, wrote this for my Instagram: "Day 100 of Korean. I can order coffee, apologize to a bus driver, and read every sign on my street. I still can't understand my girlfriend's grandmother, who speaks in dialect and laughter. Day 101 goal: the laughter." Any feedback?

Hi! I'm a junior developer and I made this joke after a rough week of code reviews: "My last pull request got the feedback 'LGTM.' I've since learned that's Latin for 'I did not open the file.'" I'm thinking of posting it on our team Slack. What's your take?

units: Our neighborhood association wants to cut down the old oak beside the church to add 14 parking spots. I'm speaking against it: "That oak is 140 years old. Parking lots get repaved every twenty years; trees can only be cut once. You can always add spaces later. You can't add a hundred and forty years." I'm 71 and not much of a public speaker. Is it enough?

I'm a herbalist who wants to build a 6m x 6m tea and medicine garden. It's a mandala, with four quadrants divided by paths: calming (chamomile, lemon balm, lavender), digestive (peppermint, fennel, calendula), immune (echinacea, elderberry, thyme), and a quadrant for rotating annuals. In the center, a small sundial surrounded by holy basil. Drying racks are on the shed's south wall. What do you make of it?

I'm a carpenter, and I wasted a lot of lumber before I wrote this out. The app is called Kerf. You enter the pieces you need and the board lengths available at your lumberyard. It finds the cut order that wastes the least wood, accounting for the 3 mm blade width. It prints a cut list with each cut numbered on a diagram of the board. Does it sound practical to you?

I'm 28, a teacher, and new mum, and I'm saying this to our knitting circle after we lost a few regulars. Feeling a bit emotional about it. How does it read? "A dropped stitch is invisible for six rows, and then it's all you can see. Same with a friend who stops coming. If you're missing someone from this circle, don't wait six rows. Pick up the phone. Pick up the stitch."

I'm a copy editor, and my cafe is called "Em Dash." The tagline on the window will read: "A pause worth taking." I wanted the name to be small and typographic and to say something about slowing down mid-sentence. I've stared at it for so long that I can't judge it anymore. Could you tell me what you think?

I'm an accountant, and I'm finally opening a cafe in a disused bank on Orchard Street. I'm calling it "Small Change." The old vault will be the seating area, and a few pence from every coffee goes to local community projects. I'm nervous about showing this to anyone. Does the name work for you? Be honest, please.

I'm a grad student and my band needs a chorus for our new single. Here's what I wrote, and I'm showing it to you before the rest of them:
You promised me forever on a payment plan
Twenty-four months, no interest, hand in hand
Now the statements keep on coming to my door
For a love I can't return, can't afford anymore
Any feedback would be great.

I've made candles as a hobby for three years. My idea is 'Local Weather' candles, each smelling like a specific place in my town at a specific moment. Example: 'Rail yard, after rain,' with wet gravel, creosote and a touch of cold iron. Each box has a map card, and $2 goes to the historical society. I'd sell 40 at the farmers market first. How does that sound to you?

I'm a beekeeper with six hives, and I planned a 10m x 10m forage garden to support them from March to October. Early: crocus, willow, and hellebores. Spring: lungwort, borage, and fruit blossoms. Summer: lime tree, phacelia, and marjoram. Autumn: ivy, Sedum, and asters. Hives are in the southeast corner, facing away from the path, with a 2m hedge forcing bees to fly up. What do you think of it?

I work closing shifts at a cinema and made a suggestion to my manager. Here's the email:
"Hi Paula, closing takes us 55 minutes because we sweep each theater after cleaning the concession counter. If one person starts on the theaters while the other counts the till, I timed it at 35 minutes in a trial last Friday. It means everyone leaves earlier and the floors get cleaned while the popcorn is still warm. Can I show you the checklist? Thanks, Devon"
What do you think?

units: I'm an urban planner with an idea called Desire Lines. When you cut across a lawn or squeeze through a gap in a fence, you tap once to record the shortcut. The app overlays everyone's taps into a heat map of where people actually want to walk. Cities could use it to put paths where feet already go. I'd really like your thoughts.

I knit as a hobby and I've been toying with a business idea. One sentence: "Knitters abandon sweaters at the sleeves because patterns don't fit their bodies, so we sell $14 pattern files that recalculate every stitch count from five measurements." Curious what you make of it, be as blunt as you like!

Hi! For my databases course I had to list every consecutive-day login streak per user. Here's my Postgres attempt:
WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, login_at::date AS d FROM logins),
g AS (SELECT user_id, d, d - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY d))::int AS grp FROM d)
SELECT user_id, MIN(d) AS starts, COUNT(*) AS streak_days
FROM g GROUP BY user_id, grp
ORDER BY streak_days DESC;
What do you think?

Serve on whipped labneh with lemon zest and garlic, scatter with homemade dukkah (hazelnut, coriander, sesame, cumin), and finish with hot honey spiked with sherry vinegar. Would this work as a starter, or is it too much going on?

units: I coach marathoners. My app is called Negative Split. Most pacing apps talk constantly, which drives me nuts. This one stays silent while you're within 5 seconds per mile of target. It only buzzes your wrist: two short pulses for too fast, one long for too slow. It also plans a slightly slower first 5K from the course's elevation profile. Can you give me feedback?

I groom dogs for a living and wanted my bio to be a little different. Could I get your thoughts?
"I spend my days making nervous dogs feel brave. I'm not saying I can do the same for you, but I'm not not saying it. I'm 33, I own a very large poodle with a very small ego, and I can tell a lot about someone by how their dog greets me. No dog? No problem, I'll take your word."

I illustrate on commission from my home studio and I'm pitching a children's book publisher. Here's the paragraph from my letter, wondering what you think.
"I draw the sort of picture a child finds on the third reading: the mouse behind the curtain, the half-eaten pear under the bed, the cat who looks guilty in every scene. My sketchbooks are full of these small secrets, and I would like to hide them in your books."

Her side of the bed—

with slow morning light

My mom said to ask someone who knows apps.

```python
def in_window(now, start, end):
    """True if now is in [start, end), even across midnight."""
    if start <= end:
        return start <= now < end
    return now >= start or now < end
```

I live on a steep slope in Cape Town, and this is my plan for terraced fynbos. Four dry-stone terraces, each 1.5m wide, with the steps offset so water never funnels down. Top terrace: proteas and leucadendrons. Middle: restios and pelargoniums. Bottom: Agapanthus and buchu near the path. No irrigation after the first summer. I'd really love your feedback on the plan!

Flowers for the bees run along the paths' edges. How does it look to you?

units: I'm a hobbyist and I'm trying out dew collection. Four 20 × 20 cm panels (aluminium, painted aluminium, plastic, and cotton) are set up on my roof at 30° overnight, and I weigh the water collected each dawn. I'm logging humidity, temperature, and sky cover, so I can compare conditions across 20 nights. Could you tell me your thoughts?

Casual question: I'm 45, sit at a desk nine hours a day, and my shoulders are creeping forward. Mon/Thu: rows, face pulls, wall angels, dead bugs. Tue/Fri: hip flexor stretch, glute bridges, goblet squats, 20-minute walk. Wed: swim or bike, whatever. Weekend: one hike. Plus a 2-minute doorway chest stretch every time my coffee finishes. Does this make sense? Roast me if needed.

I'm an undergrad writing my history honours thesis. My question is: "Why did Ottoman port authorities in Salonica begin recording ship cargoes in French in the 1880s, and what does that choice reveal about who the records were meant for?" What's your opinion?

I'm 68 and retired, and I'm sick of mosquito-repelling phone apps. For my grandson's fair, we'll build a two-chamber choice box with a screen divider, put in 20 fruit flies, and then play the app's tone on only one side. A blinded helper chooses the side with a coin flip. After 10 minutes we count the flies per side. Then we'll repeat it 30 times and run a binomial test. What's your opinion?

My grandmother takes seven pills a day and gets confused about which she's had. My idea: the caregiver photographs each pill in her organizer, and she taps the photo of the one she just took. No reading required. The family gets one quiet summary each evening, not constant alerts. I'd like to know what you think before I show it to my aunts.

I'm a student who works at a skate rink, and I spotted a hazard. This is my email to my manager:
"Hi Joan, the rubber mat by the rental counter has curled at one corner. Two kids tripped on it today, and nobody was hurt. I've put an orange cone on it and taken a photo, attached. A replacement is about $40 at the hardware store on Elm, and I can pick it up on my way in tomorrow. Okay to do that? Thanks, Sam"
What do you think?

Latest reading per sensor, for a dashboard that refreshes every few seconds. I'm an IoT hobbyist with a Raspberry Pi and a lot of sensors:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (sensor_id) sensor_id, recorded_at, temp_c
FROM readings
WHERE recorded_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
ORDER BY sensor_id, recorded_at DESC;
I also have an index on (sensor_id, recorded_at DESC). Any feedback would be great!

I've been home with my kids for 8 years and I'm applying for a project coordinator job. Nervous! Paragraph: "For eight years I've managed a team of three with unpredictable deadlines, no budget, and a 6 a.m. launch every day. I also ran the school auction, which raised $41,000 using one spreadsheet and fifty unreliable volunteers. People call that a transferable skill. I'd like to prove it on yours." Honest reaction, please?
I make alarm clocks, small batch, with a sunrise light. The line I'm testing for the box is: "Gentle enough to forgive you. Loud enough not to." What do you think?

Weekend gardener here, and my zucchini has gotten completely out of hand. I turned it into a country chorus. Be straight with me, what's your take?
Zucchini in July, please, I'm begging you stop,
I've left bags on porches, I've filled the church shop.
The neighbors all wave with a too-careful smile.
They've seen me coming up the drive for a mile.

units: Here's my woodworking budget, $120 a month. Rough lumber from the sawmill $50, blades/bits/sandpaper $15, finishes $10, tool fund $30 (one good tool at a time, currently a $180 hand plane), dust filter replacements $5, makerspace class $10. Be as blunt as you like. What do you think?

I'm a drummer and teacher. My app is Ghost Bars, a metronome that goes silent. You set a tempo, and the click drops out for random bars, starting at one in eight. As you stay steady, it slowly increases the share of silent bars. When the click returns, it shows in milliseconds how far you drifted. It's meant to train internal pulse instead of leaning on the click. Does it seem worthwhile?

I'm a Dungeon Master and posted this on r/DnD: "My players found a door that only opened if you told it the truth. Three hours later the paladin admitted he'd never liked his god, and the door was still locked. It was waiting for the rogue." Does it land for you?

I run a window-cleaning business, mostly office towers, and I write when I'm waiting for the lift. Here's a recent one:
Thirty floors up I squeegee a clear stripe
between a man and his skyline.
He doesn't look up.
I wave anyway,
one wet second of me, passing.
Could you give me some feedback?

Hey! I'm a freshman and this is my first haiku since middle school. Wrote it walking to class this morning. Any thoughts?
First snow on campus—
the whole quad forgets its paths
until we make them.

Warehouse supervisor, learning SQL at night. Stock upsert that ignores out-of-order updates from the scanners:
INSERT INTO inventory (sku, qty, updated_at)
VALUES ('A-114', 25, now())
ON CONFLICT (sku) DO UPDATE
SET qty = inventory.qty + EXCLUDED.qty,
    updated_at = EXCLUDED.updated_at
WHERE inventory.updated_at < EXCLUDED.updated_at;
I'd appreciate your opinion. Be gentle, it's my first real one!

I've been a grant writer for 12 years and I'm trying something looser for our food bank's donor letter. "Dear Ms. Alvarez, Last Tuesday a man in our line held up a can of chickpeas and asked if it was for people or for the cat. I said people. He said, 'Good. Then I'll take two.' Hunger here isn't dramatic. It's arithmetic." Thoughts?

I'm captain of our school robotics club, and we got knocked out in round two. Tomorrow I'm speaking to the team: "Our arm dropped the cube at 1:12. I've watched the footage nine times. The arm wasn't the problem; our calibration sheet hadn't been updated since October. So every Friday, someone tests what we assume. Losing in round two taught us more than winning round one would have." How does it read?
I make alarm clocks, small batch, with a sunrise light. The line I'm testing for the box is: "Gentle enough to forgive you. Loud enough not to." What do you think?

Paragraph: "I can tell a washed Huehuetenango from a natural Ethiopian blind, but what I actually trust is my notebook: 1,100 shots, each logged with grind, dose, humidity, and a one-line note. Taste fades by lunchtime. Records don't. I'd like to be the person who writes down what the rest of us forget." Thoughts?

units: I teach pottery classes as a hobby, and I'm designing a project on crazing. Same clay body and same glaze on 18 tiles. I fire them together, then cool them at three rates by cracking the kiln lid at 900°C, 700°C, or leaving it closed. I count crazing lines per cm² after 24 hours and a week. What would you say about this?

I'm nervous about this one. It's my first design: a 10x10 ft moss garden under a Japanese maple in Portland. A single weathered basalt boulder sits off-centre, with raked gravel flowing around it like a stream. Hair cap moss goes on the shaded side and cushion moss on the sunlit side. A slate stepping path bends once so you can't see the whole garden at a glance. Would you tell me what you think?

I run a pet-sitting business and I'm emailing the manager of the kennel I partner with. Here goes:
"Hi Greta, over July 4th weekend, I'd like to reserve five overflow kennels for my regular clients. All five dogs are vaccinated, and I'll send their records by Friday. I'll drop off, feed, and walk them myself, so there's no extra work for your staff. I can pay $200 up front. Could you confirm by the 20th? Thanks, Marcus"
What do you think?

I make a true crime podcast about small towns, called Dead Air. The logo is an audio waveform running across the width of the square. The peaks on the left are shaped like rooftops, a steeple, a water tower, a gabled barn, and then the line goes completely flat for the right third. White on charcoal. I'm a bit nervous posting this. How does it read to you?

Just finished my astrophysics postdoc and I'm opening a cafe between the hospital and the university. It's called "Lagrange Point," which is where two big gravitational pulls cancel out and things just stay put. That's what happens to nurses and students who come in for one coffee. Does the name come across, or is it too nerdy?

I'm three weeks into a new job and my manager asked for onboarding feedback. Here's my reply. Does it seem fair and useful?
"Hi Danielle, what's working: shadowing Kofi. What slowed me: I waited six days for system access. I've drafted a day-one checklist (attached) from what I wish I'd had. Happy to be the guinea pig for the next hire."

Nurse of 11 years trying to move into UX research. Here's my pitch paragraph, please be straight with me: "I have run roughly 40,000 usability tests, though we called them shifts. I know exactly where your charting software fails: 3 a.m., one hand gloved, during a rapid response. I can't yet build a Figma prototype as polished as yours, but I can tell you which button a frightened person will press first." What do you think?

Illustrator here, writing my first text. This is the refrain of a bedtime book:
"Not yet," said the moon, "I'm still tucking in the sea."
"Not yet," said the sea, "I'm still rocking the whale."
"Not yet," said the whale, "I'm humming the stars their tune."
"Not yet," said the stars, "we're waiting up for you."
Thoughts on how it reads aloud?

I keep aquariums, and I'm trying duckweed as a nitrate sensor. I'll grow 10 fronds per jar in 0, 5, 20, and 50 ppm nitrate, then photograph from above every day for 12 days. ImageJ gives me the green area, which I'll use to calculate the growth rate. Three replicates, same light and temperature. Could I get your opinion on it?

I'm a grad student and my band needs a chorus for our new single. Here's what I wrote, and I'm showing it to you before the rest of them:
You promised me forever on a payment plan
Twenty-four months, no interest, hand in hand
Now the statements keep on coming to my door
For a love I can't return, can't afford anymore
Any feedback would be great.

I'm part of our college radio station and we're redoing the logo. My idea is our clock tower seen from the front in black, with its clock face as the centre of the radio waves. Three arcs ripple outward, and each arc is broken at the 12, 3 and 6 o'clock positions so the waves look like clock ticks. Thoughts?

I run a small bike repair shop and I'm writing a piece for our city's business blog. Thesis: "Right-to-repair laws are usually defended on economic grounds, but their strongest case is epistemic: a society that can't open its devices gradually loses the ability to understand the things it depends on." Thoughts?

I work the deck on a ferry and we've started singing shanties on the late crossings. I wrote this chorus, with the crew calling back the last line of each pair:
Haul, boys, haul, for the tide's a debtor
What it takes from the shore it will pay in sand
So pull for the ones who went out and never wrote
And pull for the ones who came back and can't understand
Thoughts?

I'm an urban planner with an idea called Desire Lines. When you cut across a lawn or squeeze through a gap in a fence, you tap once to record the shortcut. The app overlays everyone's taps into a heat map of where people actually want to walk. Cities could use it to put paths where feet already go. I'd really like your thoughts.

Drama club president here! We need $2,500 to stage Our Town. My opening: "We will perform a play with no scenery in a gym with too much of it: banners, bleachers, a scoreboard stuck at 42–38. Our Town asks the audience to imagine everything. We only need lights, a rented ladder, and you." Tell me what you think?

I'm 14 and I like music, so I'm doing Chladni plates. I'm bolting a 20 cm square aluminum plate to a speaker driver, sprinkling salt on it, and sweeping frequencies from 100 to 3000 Hz. I'll photograph each pattern at resonance, then compare the frequencies to the theoretical plate-mode formula to find which ones match. I'll also test how the patterns change when I clamp the plate at its center vs. its edge. What do you think?

Bootcamp student here. I needed to turn nested config into flat keys and ended up with this recursive version. How would you rate it?
```js
const flat = (o, p = '') =>
  Object.entries(o).flatMap(([k, v]) =>
    v && typeof v === 'object' ? flat(v, p + k + '.') : [[p + k, v]]);
Object.fromEntries(flat({ a: { b: 1, c: { d: 2 } } }));
```
I own a hardware store that my grandfather started. For our new sign I wrote: "Hardware store. Software optional." I'd love to know what you think.

I'm a new dad (38) and I wrote this lullaby chorus at 3 a.m. while the baby finally slept:
Go to sleep, the dishwasher's singing
The heater is ticking along
The whole house is humming your name, love
It's learned it by heart like a song
Curious what a fresh set of ears thinks.

I'm a tailor, and my book is about trousers. "Hem" follows one pair of corduroys across three brothers. Each page the hem is let down an inch, and the pockets hold what the last boy left: a pebble, a bus ticket, a dried worm. On the final page the youngest hears the jingle and realizes he's wearing his brothers' whole childhoods. Tell me what you think!

I moved here from Vietnam eight years ago. My idea is Backpack Letter. You photograph any school letter or form. It tells you in Vietnamese, or another language you choose, what the letter is about, what you have to do, and the deadline. Then it adds the deadline to your calendar, with a reminder two days before. It never translates word for word. It says things like "They need a signature, not money." I'd like your opinion.

I live on a steep slope in Cape Town, and this is my plan for terraced fynbos. Four dry-stone terraces, each 1.5m wide, with the steps offset so water never funnels down. Top terrace: proteas and leucadendrons. Middle: restios and pelargoniums. Bottom: Agapanthus and buchu near the path. No irrigation after the first summer. I'd really love your feedback on the plan!

I'm a freelance translator and I've made a joke about my marriage: "Being married to a translator means every argument ends with 'Well, that's not what the original said.'" My husband has asked me not to put it in my newsletter. Do you think I should?

I work closing shifts at a cinema and made a suggestion to my manager. Here's the email:
"Hi Paula, closing takes us 55 minutes because we sweep each theater after cleaning the concession counter. If one person starts on the theaters while the other counts the till, I timed it at 35 minutes in a trial last Friday. It means everyone leaves earlier and the floors get cleaned while the popcorn is still warm. Can I show you the checklist? Thanks, Devon"
What do you think?

Pitching my D&D group on the next campaign: "You're all accountants to the villains. Nobody swings a sword. Every fireball comes with an invoice, the dragon's hoard needs an audit, and the Dark Lord will be furious about Q3. Trust me, the most terrifying thing in any dungeon is a well-organized ledger." Would this get you to say yes, or should I tone down the absurdity?

Here's my logline. I'm a long-haul trucker, 50, and I write in the cab at rest stops: "With six hours to his deadline, a trucker picks up a hitchhiker who can tell him exactly how many miles he has left to live, and it's fewer than the distance to his daughter's wedding." Thoughts?

Retired baker, still experimenting. Rye and caraway sourdough discard crackers: 150g discard, 60g rye flour, 40g olive oil, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp caraway seeds. Mix, rest 30 minutes, roll paper thin, brush with water, and sprinkle with flaky salt and more seeds. Bake at 180°C for 18 minutes, rotating once, until they're deep amber and snap. I'd like a second opinion, please.

I'm an urban planning student and I write a commuter blog. Title: "Mapping the Number 9 Bus." First sentence: "The 9 crosses eleven neighborhoods in forty minutes, which means that every morning I travel through three tax brackets, two languages, and one very opinionated pigeon." Okay, be honest: what's your reaction to this?

Algorithms class homework: write a prime sieve. This is my version. Any comments?
```python
def primes_up_to(n):
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i*i::i] = bytes(len(range(i*i, n + 1, i)))
    return [i for i, p in enumerate(sieve) if p]
```

units:
I'm a taxi driver, 40, and I moved here eleven years ago. I've been turning my feelings into songs. This is the chorus of the newest:
I wear two watches, one for here, one for home
One says it's noon, one says you're asleep
I live in the hours that don't have a name
Keeping time for the ones I can't keep
I'd be grateful for your opinion.

I teach high school drama and I'm writing a musical about a stagehand. This is her big chorus:
Somebody's got to stand in the dark
So the star can find her mark
I'm the tape on the floor, the ghost light's spark
I'm the reason you won't fall
And I'm not in the program at all
I'd love your opinion before I show the cast.

Language-learning student here, wrote this for my Instagram: "Day 100 of Korean. I can order coffee, apologize to a bus driver, and read every sign on my street. I still can't understand my girlfriend's grandmother, who speaks in dialect and laughter. Day 101 goal: the laughter." Any feedback?

I run a small bakery and I'm mentoring a student with this idea. Sourdough starter in identical clear jars, same flour and hydration, held at 18, 22, 26 and 30°C in water baths. Time-lapse photos mark rise height every 10 minutes. Then we compute peak-rise time and estimate Q10 for fermentation. Three jars per temperature. How would you rate the approach?

I'm a 62-year-old dairy farmer. At my neighbor Walt's retirement, I said: 'Walt farmed the same hundred and sixty acres as his father. People call that standing still. But I watched him walk that fence line every morning for forty years, and the ground under him changed more than any of us did. You don't stay in one place by not moving. You stay by tending.' Honest feedback welcome.

I'm 61 and a member of our amateur radio club. I'm giving a short talk at the anniversary evening. Could you give me your opinion? "At 2 a.m., someone in Tasmania heard my call sign and replied, 'Good evening, Yorkshire.' Four watts, a wire in my loft, and the curvature of the Earth politely stepping aside. In a world of billions of messages, I still love the thirty seconds when two strangers agree to listen."

Pascal's triangle as an infinite generator. I just love how the zip trick works out, and I'm a 52-year-old accountant who picked up Python during lockdown:
```python
def pascal():
    row = [1]
    while True:
        yield row
        row = [a + b for a, b in zip([0] + row, row + [0])]
```
What do you make of it?

I own a tiny skate shop and I'm not great at talking about myself, but here's my attempt. What do you think?
"I sell skateboards to teenagers and have been told 'that's cringe' by every one of them. I'm 31, I still eat it on ledges, and I keep a first aid kit in my truck for exactly that reason. Looking for someone who'll film my attempts and not post the bad ones."

Philosophy grad student here. Here's my thesis for a seminar paper: "The trolley problem endures not because it reveals our moral intuitions but because it strips away the substance of moral life, relationships of prior obligation, so its answers describe only how people behave toward strangers they will never meet." Where would you push on it?

I'm a volunteer firefighter and this is my pitch for a side business: "We sell rural fire departments a $4,000-a-year subscription that replaces paper pre-incident plans with drone-mapped 3D layouts of every farm, so crews know where the anhydrous ammonia tank and the old propane shed are before the truck arrives." Be honest, what's your take?

Monthly cohort retention for our subscription app. I'm a data scientist and wrote it in one sitting, so tell me if I've missed something.
WITH f AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(date_trunc('month', ordered_at)) AS cohort
  FROM orders GROUP BY 1)
SELECT f.cohort,
  DATEDIFF('month', f.cohort, date_trunc('month', o.ordered_at)) AS months_since,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS active
FROM f JOIN orders o USING (customer_id)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2;

I drive long-haul and write on my phone at truck stops. Just finished the start of a blog post, "Weigh Station Poetry." It goes: "Between Amarillo and nowhere, the CB starts to sound like a congregation, forty strangers trading weather and warnings in a language none of us admitted we were inventing." Tell me what you make of it?

For my sociology seminar: "Bureaucratic waiting is usually dismissed as inefficiency, but it functions as power: by treating the citizen's time as cheap and the state's as precious, the DMV queue teaches people their place in the relationship before a single form is stamped." I'd appreciate any feedback on the thesis.

I'm a bassist who's been touring for ten years and this has happened to me twice. "When a band's player gets sick the night before a gig, we get a vetted session musician who has already studied their charts and setlist into the van within twelve hours." What do you think?

I moved here from Vietnam eight years ago. My idea is Backpack Letter. You photograph any school letter or form. It tells you in Vietnamese, or another language you choose, what the letter is about, what you have to do, and the deadline. Then it adds the deadline to your calendar, with a reminder two days before. It never translates word for word. It says things like "They need a signature, not money." I'd like your opinion.

I own a laundromat, and last month I added an espresso bar in the front corner. I'm calling the whole place "Delicates." The sign would be hand-painted, cold-water-wash-label style. Curious what you make of it!

I run a little toy shop and wrote a fable for the kids who come in on Saturdays. Here's how it begins. Would you tell me what you think? "Once there was a clock that was always seven minutes slow, and the town loved it for exactly that reason. Late for church? Blame the clock. Late for love? The clock. It carried the town's small sins like a mule, until the day a clockmaker arrived, tool bag in hand, offering to help."

I'm a college freshman, and my aunt Rosa is retiring from our family farm. I'm giving the speech: "Aunt Rosa gets up at 4:30 because the cows don't read calendars. I used to think that was sad. Now I think it's the most honest schedule I know: someone needs you, so you show up. Forty years, no vacations, a full table every Sunday. Rosa, rest. The cows will understand. We won't, but we'll try." Thoughts?

units: Soup dumplings from scratch, my weekend project. Filling: 500g pork with 30% fat, ginger-scallion water added in three batches and stirred in one direction, then 300g cold pork-skin aspic, cubed and folded in. Wrappers: hot-water dough, rolled thin at the edges and thicker in the centre, 18 pleats. Steam 8 minutes on cabbage leaves. What would you improve?

I'm a marine biologist and I'm starting a company called Shell Game. We pick up oyster shells from restaurants weekly, a fee of $30 a month, cure them for six months and deliver them to reef restoration projects. Each restaurant receives a plaque: "Your shells built 3 square feet of reef." Photos and GPS coordinates are included each quarter. Would restaurants actually pay? Curious what you think.

We run a small vegetable farm with a CSA of 60 members. My idea: members can swap items in their box until Wednesday night, like trading kale for extra carrots. The app then sends us a harvest list adjusted by swaps, so we pick what's wanted. It also shows a 'surplus' list for cheap add-ons. Could you tell me what you think?

I lead HR for a call center and I'm applying for a VP role. One bullet I've gone back and forth on: "Redesigned frontline hiring for a 600-employee center, replacing resume screens with 20-minute work-sample calls; 90-day attrition fell from 41% to 19%, saving roughly $730K annually." What's your honest opinion?

I'm an undergrad raising $3,000 to sequence soil from my grandmother's farm. Here's my opening, and I'm a bit anxious about it: "My grandmother says the south field is tired. I study microbes, so I asked what tired means. A teaspoon of that soil holds billions of organisms, and I'd like to find out which ones have quit." How does it land for you?

I'm a grad student, writing a short story about my grandmother. Sharing the first paragraph with some nerves: "The telegram came on a Tuesday, which my grandmother held against Tuesdays for the rest of her life. She forgave the postman, the war, and eventually God. But Tuesdays she kept, the way a dog keeps a bone, and so for sixty years, every week, we ate cold supper and did not answer the door." What do you think?

I drive the Route 9 bus and write poems on my breaks. This is from the last run of the night. What do you think?
Route 9, final run. The bus exhales.
Rows of seats keep the shapes of strangers,
a dent here, a warmth there,
and I drive the empty ghosts back to the depot
with my headlights on for them.

Nurse of 11 years trying to move into UX research. Here's my pitch paragraph, please be straight with me: "I have run roughly 40,000 usability tests, though we called them shifts. I know exactly where your charting software fails: 3 a.m., one hand gloved, during a rapid response. I can't yet build a Figma prototype as polished as yours, but I can tell you which button a frightened person will press first." What do you think?

Our bakery chalkboard and website need a line for the bread everyone asks about. This is what I wrote: "Sourdough Boule, 900 g. Thirty-six-hour ferment, stone-ground Ontario wheat, a crust that crackles under your thumb and a crumb open enough to hold butter in pools. Baked Tuesday to Saturday, gone by noon. Reserve yours the night before." Can you tell me what you think?
so my brother and I started a small tea company in our garage and this is the slogan I drafted lol: "Sit down. It's steeping." Be honest, what do you think?

units:
Pareto analysis for our catalogue: what share of revenue the top products make. I added the tie-breaker and ROWS frame deliberately.
WITH r AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(revenue) AS rev FROM sales GROUP BY product_id)
SELECT product_id, rev,
  SUM(rev) OVER (ORDER BY rev DESC, product_id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) / SUM(rev) OVER () AS cum_share
FROM r ORDER BY rev DESC, product_id;
I'm a finance manager, not a developer. Does this look right to you?

I'm a literary translator replying to a post claiming AI will make us obsolete: "Translation isn't swapping words. It's deciding what to lose. Every sentence of Chekhov costs something in English, and someone has to choose the price. A machine can hand you the menu. It can't tell you which dish to give up, or sit with you while you grieve it." Posting this tonight. Would you share it?

I teach seventh grade and wrote this on the staffroom whiteboard today: "Teaching teenagers is like being a human Wi-Fi router: everyone's staring at me, nobody's connected, and the moment I move, they complain about the signal." Curious what people outside teaching make of it.

I'm 40 and a T10 paraplegic. I want to build strength without wrecking my shoulders. Mon: seated cable rows 4x10, face pulls 3x15, landmine press 3x8. Tue: handcycle intervals, 6x2 min hard/2 easy. Wed: rest. Thu: lat pulldowns 4x8, parallel-bar dips 3x6, rotator cuff band work. Fri: 30-minute steady handcycle. Sat: Pallof presses and core. Sun: rest. Pulling volume is double pushing on purpose. Thoughts?

I'm 20, a sophomore working at a campus café. Monthly money is $1,150. Room 520; groceries 180 (Sunday batch cooking); phone 25; textbook fund 50; laundry 20; coffee and friends 80; savings 100; tuition-gap fund 100; clothes 25; unassigned 50. First budget I've ever made. Does it look okay to you? Any advice appreciated!

I do open mics on Thursdays as a hobby, and this is my new opener: "I slept wrong once in 2019 and my neck is still in litigation." I'm tempted to follow it with nothing, just let it sit. Does that instinct make sense? Genuinely curious.

I'm an architect and wrote this on LinkedIn about a library we just finished: "Every building is an argument. This library says: sit down, nobody's selling you anything. That's why the windows are low. We designed them so a child could watch the rain from a beanbag." My colleagues said it was fine, but they're my friends. What do you honestly think?

I'm a 31-year-old firefighter preparing for our annual physical agility test. Mon: stair climbs in a 20 kg vest, 5x3 minutes. Tue: sled drags 6x20 m, farmer carries 4x40 m. Wed: 40-minute easy run. Thu: cable hose-pull simulation 5x30 s, dummy drags. Fri: heavy deadlifts 5x3. Sat: full timed test circuit. Sun: rest, foam roll. Does this seem right to you?

I dispatch buses and write short emails. This one's for my manager. Opinion?
"Hi Pat, route 14's 7:40 is always 8 minutes late because the school crossing on Elm adds traffic. Drivers have logged it for three weeks. Move the timetable to 7:48 and the complaint calls stop. It costs nothing. Thanks, Ruth."

I'm a sonar-tech student, and I tried writing a drama about it. "A submarine sonar operator realizes the whale she has tracked for years is singing her late father's navy radio call sign, and that the pattern has begun to count down." Would you mind giving me your opinion?

units: I teach physics and I'm opening our astronomy society's autumn meeting with this. "Vega's light left in the year our newest member was born, so tonight, when you look up, you're seeing Vega as a toddler. Every observing night is time travel with bad coffee. Bring a flask, bring a child, and let's go meet the past together." Could you tell me what you make of it?

I run a small bakery in Tulsa and wrote this for a local business grant application: "We freeze tomorrow's unsold sourdough at closing and sell it as a $12 rescue box to restaurants for croutons and bread pudding, turning our 15% waste into a profit line." Would you give me your feedback?

I run a four-person plumbing company. Dale's retiring after 40 years and I'm ending my speech with this: "Dale has been in more basements than anyone in this county and never repeated a single secret he found there. People meet us on their worst day, wet and panicking, and we leave them dry and dignified. Dale, thanks for teaching me the real trade is trust. The pipes are easy." Does that land?

I'm 80 and my granddaughter said I should show someone. It's a story from my childhood, dressed up a bit:
"The summer I was nine, the circus came to Ballina and left without its elephant. Nobody could explain it. She stood in Mr. Doyle's field for six weeks, enormous and patient, eating his hay, until the whole parish had told her something it had never told another living soul."
What do you think, dear?

I'm applying for a historical marker for the old Delmar Bakery on 5th Street. Our statement opens: "For 41 years this building fed the neighborhood on credit. A ledger still hangs on the back wall, recording striking miners' debts the owner never collected. Towns are remembered for their monuments, but they're held together by their bakeries." How does it read to you?

I'm Nigerian, studying in Leeds, and this is my party jollof. Blend roasted red peppers, tomatoes, scotch bonnet and onion, then fry the base in oil for about 25 minutes until it separates. Add thyme, curry powder, bay and stock. Parboiled rice, sealed with foil under the lid, finishing on low so the bottom catches lightly. Butter at the end. How does the method read to you?

For my sociology seminar: "Bureaucratic waiting is usually dismissed as inefficiency, but it functions as power: by treating the citizen's time as cheap and the state's as precious, the DMV queue teaches people their place in the relationship before a single form is stamped." For my marketing class I invented an alarm clock that wakes you with gradual sunlight. My slogan is "Sunrise, minus the rooster." Can you give me feedback? My professor wants peer opinions.

Nervous about sharing this, but here's the thesis for my game design class essay: "Tetris endures not because it is simple but because it is unwinnable: its design turns inevitable failure into a measure of skill, teaching players to take pleasure in managing loss rather than avoiding it." Would love your reaction.
I run a used bookshop and wanted something for our window. I wrote: "Every book here has already been somebody's favourite." Tell me what you think, please. Be as blunt as you like.

I keep bees, and I sell honey at the farmers' market, so I mapped a forage plan for my 1-acre lot. A six-foot hedge of serviceberry and pussy willow sits in front of the hives to force a high flight path. Bloom runs in order: willow in March, crocus, then lilac, then basswood, then borage and buckwheat in July. Asters and goldenrod go in for autumn. A shallow water dish with pebbles sits 10 ft from the hives. Does it look sensible?

I'm cataloguing my vinyl collection in Postgres with a tags array. Wanted live jazz albums but no Christmas ones:
CREATE INDEX albums_tags_gin ON albums USING gin (tags);
SELECT title, artist
FROM albums
WHERE tags @> ARRAY['jazz', 'live']
  AND NOT tags && ARRAY['christmas']
ORDER BY artist, title;
I'd love to know how this strikes you.

Just finished this chorus and I'm kind of buzzing, so I'm sharing it right away. I'm a senior in high school, and it's about my town. Tell me what you think!
Everybody here knows my middle name and my mother's,
the truck my dad sold, the fence I drove through.
I'm leaving in June with one bag and no one's blessing.
God, I hope someplace else knows me half as well as you.

Mom of three, so my workouts ride on existing routines. Mon: while the pasta boils, 3 rounds of 10 squats and 10 counter push-ups. Tue: school-run walk, pushing the stroller up the big hill. Wed: during swim lessons, 30 laps. Thu: 20-minute kettlebell video while the kids watch a show. Fri: 15-minute kitchen dance party. Sat: family hike carrying the youngest. Sun: rest. Does this seem sustainable?

I run a food truck downtown and write haiku on my lunch break. Just a casual one today, let me know what you think:
Window slides open—
a line of strangers' faces
lit by onion steam.

I'm a sysadmin and I've been burned by half-written config files, so I made this:
```python
def atomic_write(path, data):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=d)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
            f.write(data)
            f.flush()
            os.fsync(f.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except BaseException:
        os.unlink(tmp)
        raise
```
What's your opinion?

```python
def in_window(now, start, end):
    """True if now is in [start, end), even across midnight."""
    if start <= end:

    return now >= start or now < end
```

Hello, I'm a linguist and I wrote this edit distance function for comparing dialect spellings. It only keeps one row in memory:
```python
def levenshtein(a, b):
    prev = range(len(b) + 1)
    for i, ca in enumerate(a, 1):
        cur = [i]
        for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
            cur.append(min(prev[j] + 1, cur[j-1] + 1, prev[j-1] + (ca != cb)))
        prev = cur
    return prev[-1]
```
Could you give me your opinion?

units:
I own a little flower shop and wrote this on my lunch break. Showing it to you first, before anyone I know:
I can tell which bouquets will be forgiven
by how the man holds them:
like a question,
or like an alibi.
How does it read to you?

I'm a college freshman, and my aunt Rosa is retiring from our family farm. I'm giving the speech: "Aunt Rosa gets up at 4:30 because the cows don't read calendars. I used to think that was sad. Now I think it's the most honest schedule I know: someone needs you, so you show up. Forty years, no vacations, a full table every Sunday. Rosa, rest. The cows will understand. We won't, but we'll try." Thoughts?

Environmental science major here. My thesis for the policy paper: "Carbon offsets fail not because forests burn but because they sell a permanent license for a temporary promise: a ton emitted today stays in the atmosphere for centuries, while the tree that 'cancels' it can be cut down next decade." Thoughts?

I'm 81 and this is the first poem I've ever shown anyone. My granddaughter set up this chat for me. I'd be glad to hear what you think.
At eighty I price the stairs by breath:
the fourth one costs a nickel,
the ninth, a dime.
I reach the landing, solvent still,
and spend what's left on the window.

I'm a retired cabinetmaker, 68, and my daughter talked me into a dating site. Here's the bio: "I can tell what's wrong with your drawers by the sound they make. Widowed three years, ready for company that argues about whether the crossword is cheating if you look up one answer. I make soup on Sundays, always too much. Bring a bowl and an opinion on dovetails." What do you make of it?

I own a used bookstore, and my clerk Miriam retires after 21 years. Draft of my toast: "Miriam can look at a stranger for three seconds and hand them the book they didn't know they were missing. I've watched her do it nine hundred times and never seen her wrong. She'd call it luck. I call it a kind of love. We stock forty thousand books. Miriam, you were the one worth recommending." Feedback?

Apprentice electrician, just finished my hours and building my first resume. Here's what I wrote: "Completed 8,000 apprenticeship hours with zero recordable safety incidents; independently ran conduit and terminated a 400A service for a 24-unit apartment retrofit, passing inspection on the first visit." What do you think?

Here's the opening line of my historical novel, set in 1880s Hungary: "The year the river changed its mind, my father sold our cow, our name, and nearly me." I'm a history student and I've been staring at this one for ages. Any feedback would be welcome.

I own a flower shop and I'm training for my first marathon (week 10 of 16). Mon: rest. Tue: 8 miles easy. Wed: 6 miles with 3x1 mile at tempo. Thu: 5 easy plus strides, 20 min strength. Fri: rest. Sat: 16 mile long run, last 3 at goal pace. Sun: 4 recovery miles. Wedding season hits in May, so Fridays stay empty on purpose. What's your take?

units:
I drive the night bus on the number 14 route. I've been jotting haiku on my break for years. Here's one I finally typed up:
Last bus, rain-streaked glass—
each passenger's face lit once
by passing streetlights
What would you say about it?

I'm a 20-year-old intern and somehow I was asked to speak for our founder. I said: 'I've known Mr. Reyes for eleven weeks. In that time he learned my name, my coffee order, and the name of my cat. I'm told he also started a company. I'll take people's word for it. But anyone who remembers the intern's cat has already built something that lasts.' Was that too bold?

I make a small podcast about local history from my closet, and I'm applying for a radio producer job. Here's the paragraph on my work. Can you tell me what you think?
"Episode 14 is eleven minutes about the 1952 flood, and nine of them are one woman, Dolores, describing the sound of the river at night. I cut my own questions to almost nothing. A producer's job, I've learned, is to build a quiet room and then leave it."

Food truck owner here, and this is my salsa macha: toast 1 cup peanuts, 3 tbsp sesame seeds, and 6 chiles de árbol and 4 guajillos in 1 cup of neutral oil on low until fragrant and just darkening. Cool, then add 4 cloves roasted garlic, 1 tbsp piloncillo, 1 tsp dried orange peel, 1 tbsp cider vinegar and salt. Pulse it chunky. It goes on everything. Thoughts?

Here's one I've been saving for my chess club's newsletter: "My chess rating is like my houseplants: technically alive, and no one is sure why." I'm pretty nervous about sharing it since some of those guys are brutal. How would you rate it?

I'm 16 and I'd like to redo Eratosthenes. I teamed up with a student at a school 410 km due north of mine through an online club. On the same day at local solar noon, we each measure a vertical stick's shadow and compute the sun angle, then use the angle difference and the distance to estimate Earth's circumference. I'll also propagate the measurement uncertainty to see whether we can tell our answer apart from 40,075 km. Thoughts?

I drive long-haul and write on the notes app at truck stops. This one came to me in Nebraska. What's your take?
Nebraska takes an hour to finish a sentence.
The grain elevators raise their one white word
and drop it behind me.
Somewhere past Kearney I say your name
to the windshield, which holds it a mile and lets go.

I'm a vegan and only a year into cooking. These are king oyster "scallops": cut stems into 2 cm thick rounds, score the tops in a crosshatch, and sear in a dry cast iron pan with a weight on top until deep brown. Then add olive oil and white miso whisked with lemon, and baste for 1 minute. Serve on pea purée with chive oil. How does it sound to you?

I'm 38, newly divorced, and my sister made me write one of these. Here's what I came up with. What's your reaction?
"Recently learned to cook for one without making enough for four. Looking for someone to help me fail at that. I own too many cast iron pans, one very old cat, and a strong opinion about rice. Funny in person, quieter in text. Come find out which."

I'm a junior in chemistry and I'm putting together a pitch for a competition. Here's my one sentence: "Universities auction off decommissioned lab equipment for pennies, so we recondition and calibrate it, certify it, and sell forty-year-old spectrometers to high school and community college labs at a tenth of the price of new." Any feedback?

units: I'm 21, nine months post-ACL reconstruction, and my physio cleared me for return-to-sport work. Mon: single-leg press 4x8 with a 3-second lower, Nordics 3x5. Tue: low box jumps with stuck landings 4x5, deceleration drills. Thu: heavy RDLs, hip thrusts. Fri: straight-line runs 6x60 m at 80%. Sat: pool. Wed/Sun: off. Hop tests are next month, so I'm tracking limb symmetry. Feedback?

Hello, I'm a brewer starting Low Tide Brewing. The logo is a pint glass in outline. The foam line at the top is a flat horizon, and below it, the beer is filled with faint sand ripples, the pattern left on a beach when the water goes out. One line weight throughout, cream on navy. I'd really like your take on it.

I'm a tailor with a small shop and I wrote this bio to sound like me. Could you tell me what you think of it?
"I fix other people's clothes for a living, so I notice when a sleeve is half an inch too long. I promise I'm not judging, just measuring. I'm 41, funny at the right moment, and slow to leave a good dinner. Looking for someone who'll let me hem their favorite jeans and tell me a story while I do."

i'm in 8th grade and my teacher said to pick a problem at our school. my thesis is: "Our cafeteria throws away about forty pounds of untouched food daily, and the cause isn't picky eaters but a twenty-minute lunch period that ends before students finish, so lunch should be lengthened before any composting program is considered." what do you think?

I roast coffee in my garage and I'm calling the brand Longitude. The logo is one coffee bean in dark espresso brown. The centre crease is a straight meridian line running top to bottom. A tiny dot sits on it, showing the exact spot of my town's coordinates, and the numbers are printed small underneath. Tell me what you think.

I knit as a hobby and I've been toying with a business idea. One sentence: "Knitters abandon sweaters at the sleeves because patterns don't fit their bodies, so we sell $14 pattern files that recalculate every stitch count from five measurements." Curious what you make of it, be as blunt as you like!

Accountant, 38, trying to switch into film production accounting. How's this paragraph? "I've audited a hospital, a shipping company, and a minor-league baseball team, and the most honest ledger belonged to the baseball team's snack stand. I like small chaos with receipts. Give me forty crew, cash per diems, and a location that changes on Thursday, and I'll hand you books that balance by Friday."

I'm a baker who codes on the side, and this turns recipe timings like "1h 30m" into milliseconds for my proofing timer. Thoughts?
```js
const units = { d: 864e5, h: 36e5, m: 6e4, s: 1e3 };
const toMs = str =>
  [...str.matchAll(/(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([dhms])/g)]
    .reduce((t, [, n, u]) => t + n * units[u], 0);
```

Here's my thesis for my music studies seminar, would appreciate your feedback: "Hip-hop sampling is best understood not as theft or homage but as citation: producers like J Dilla built arguments out of other records the way scholars build them out of footnotes." Where would you push me next?

I'm a software engineer and I've planned a 5m x 7m garden inspired by Japanese design, but adapted to Ohio. The idea: three clustered stones in an area of raked gravel, shaped like a dry stream. It's crossed by a flat stone bridge. A Japanese maple stands in the corner, and I've placed moss under a shaded eave. I'm keeping the plant list to nine species, and nothing is symmetrical. Here's the plan. What do you think?
